                                 City Council Meeting Agenda
                                      September 14, 2026
In accordance with the Open Public Meetings Act (OPMA), the Vancouver City Council meeting will be open to
in-person attendance. Options for viewing and/or participating in the meeting remotely will also be
accommodated. The City Council will be attending this meeting in person.

All City Council workshops and meetings are broadcast onCVTV cable channels 23 / HD 323 and
on www.cvtv.org.

Public testimony will be accepted regarding any matter on the agenda below. Advance registration will be
required.

Unless otherwise announced by the Presiding Officer, each speaker may testify once for up to three minutes
under each public testimony opportunity below and will be asked to provide their name and city of residence for
the record.

Testimony will be accepted in the following manner:

     • Written comments submitted in advance: Email comments to the City Council until 12:00 p.m.
       September 14, 2026. Comments will be compiled and sent to the City Council and entered into the
       record.
     • In-person or remote testimony during the meeting: Register in-person at City Hall. In-person
       registration is open until 6:30 p.m. on September 14, 2026. Instructions will be provided on-site.
       Register to testify online. Online registration is open until 12:00 p.m. on September 14, 2026.


Visit the city's website for more information and to register under Community Testimony or call the City
Manager's Office at (360) 487-8600.

Further instructions for accessing the virtual meeting (for remote testimony) will be provided upon registration.

Upon request, printouts of agenda materials will be provided, including large print.

Fee Overview
Projects typically incur a range
of fees
• Impact Fees – Parks, Traffic & Schools
• System Development Charges (SDCs) –
  Water & Sewer
• Plan Review Fees – Development Review &
  Fire
• Permit Fees – Development Review & Fire
• Inspection Fees – Development Review &
  Fire
• Miscellaneous Fees – e.g., State fee


 2 | Development Fee Update
                                            Page 8 of 578
Impact Fees & SDCs Overview
•      One-time fees charged new development to pay
       for the cost of public infrastructure needed to
       serve new residents and businesses
•      Designed to have growth pay for itself rather
       than burdening existing taxpayers
•      Funds improvements that add new capacity to
       the existing network, not for existing deficiencies
•      Calculated based on the projected demand a
       new project creates and planned capital
       investments over the next 20 years.
•      Kept in separate accounts and restricted to
       designated capital improvements


    3 | Development Fee Update
                                                             Page 9 of 578
Permit and Plan Review
Fees
•    Distinct from Impact Fees and SDCs
•    Fees paid to cover costs of processing
     and reviewing development applications,
     and inspecting construction activity
•    Calculated based on cost recovery model
     including staff, systems and transaction
     fees; time is tracked by staff and
     periodically reviewed
•    Costs include review by staff across
     multiple City departments, including
     CDD, Public Works and Fire

    7 | Development Fee Update

Why Consider Updates Now?
The City risks underfunding necessary infrastructure
• Impact Fees and SDC rates have not been adjusted in recent years despite
  increasing costs of required infrastructure projects and growing backlog.
• Comprehensive Plan update includes new growth forecasts and an updated
  Capital Facilities Plan to serve growth over the next 20 years.
• State law changes require calculation of impact fees based on proportionate
  impact.
• Commercial and industrial development does not share burden of new open
  space investments.

Impacts on New Development
Any increase in fees will make new development more expensive

• Existing market conditions not conducive to absorbing significant fee increases due
  to rising construction costs and stagnating rent

• Fees typically make up a larger percentage of development costs in smaller projects
  (middle housing)

• Increases will negatively impact residential developments, commercial, and
  industrial projects

• Slower development may result in reduced revenue to City

12 | Development Fee Update
                                                                                  Page 18 of 578
Implementation Scenarios
Fee increases can be implemented to mitigate impact on new development

• Full increases vs capped increase shared among all fee types
• Immediate increase vs phased increase over multiple years
• Pause new increases until market conditions improve
• Expand discounts and exemptions – as allowed by statute – to cover more types of
  development – affordable housing, child-care, transit-oriented development
• KEY – Find balance between potential impacts to development and being able to
  fund necessary infrastructure projects

Example Code Update
Removal of outdated language
VCM 19.11.040 - Rates in public off-street facilities
A. There is hereby established a maximum daily parking rate of $25.00, a maximum monthly parking rate of
$200.00, and a maximum event rate of $25.00 per event stay. These rates may be reduced administratively by the
city manager, or his/her their designee, pursuant to the guidelines below:

B. Any citizen 62 years of age, or older, may receive a “senior citizen discount” in an amount to be determined by
the city manager or his/her their designee, but in no event should the discount exceed 20 percent;

D. The parking rates may be changed to an amount to reach desired occupancy rates at parking meters payment
collection devices;

The city manager, or his/her their designee, is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations regarding the
administrative reduction of the maximum parking rates. The city manager, or his/her their designee, shall report
to the city council from time to time as requested by the city council, but in any event, shall report at least once
every year regarding these parking rates.

Scofflaw Program
The lack of a scofflaw program allows a small group to abuse system

• Provides accountability for vehicles with multiple parking infractions.
• Equalizes authority to enforce in-state and out-of-state vehicles.
• Improves compliance with on-street parking regulations.
• Reduces the current number of delinquent or scofflaw vehicles.
• Reduces the number of boots and tows required after the first year by
  increasing payment compliance.
• Harmonizes off-street and on-street authority.




6 | VMC Title 19 Code Update
                                                                            Page 27 of 578
Scofflaw Program
Definitions

• Scofflaw refers to a vehicle which habitually and contemptuously breaks the
  law without concern for the consequences.

• 4 or more citations unpaid for 45 or more days.

• 3 additional notice and due process steps.

• Addition of immobilization devices (boots) and impoundment as enforcement
  tools.

7 | VMC Title 19 Code Update
                                                                           Page 28 of 578
Scofflaw Program
Current Authority
• RCW 46.16A.120
     o Prohibits vehicle registration in Washington only if there are any outstanding standing,
       stopping, and parking violations.
• RCW 46.55.113
     o Allows impound of a vehicle with registration expired by 45 days or more.
• VMC 19.13.080
     o “Subject to other monetary penalties provided by law including, but not limited to,
       referral to a collection agency.”
• No additional enforcement options are available to address delinquent fines
  associated with out-of-state or no-plate vehicles. These vehicles account for
  47% of all unpaid fines.

a Vancouver city ordinance by this reference.

It is further provided that the Washington Model Traffic Ordinance and this title
and other ordinances as referred to herein shall together constitute and be

                                                                                Page 37 of 578
                                 Chapter 19.02
                           PURPOSE AND POLICY

19.02.010     Exercise of police power.

This entire chapter title shall be deemed and construed to be an exercise of the
police power of the City of Vancouver in the state of Washington for the
preservation and protection of public safety, and all of its provisions shall be
liberally construed with a view to the effectuation of such purpose.

19.02.020    Regulatory purpose.

The coins required to be deposited in payment collected by payment collection
devices and the permit fees as provided herein are levied and assessed as fees to
provide for the proper regulation and control of traffic upon the public streets
and to cover the cost of the supervision, inspection, installation, operation,
maintenance, control and use of the parking spaces and parking meters payment
collection devices described herein, the cost of supervising and regulating the
parking of vehicles in the parking meter zones, and the cost of issuing the delivery
permits and identification cards.

19.02.030    General duty.

Nothing in this Title is intended to create a cause of action or claim against the
City of Vancouver or its officials, employees or agents running to specific
individuals. Any duty created by the ordinances codified in this chapter is a
general duty running in favor of the public.

19.02.040    Limited parking.

A. Purpose Authorized. For the purpose of facilitating the movement of traffic
and access to the business districts of the city and providing just and equitable



                                                                                     Page 38 of 578
parking privileges and opportunities for operators of motor vehicles, the city
traffic engineer may impose time limits upon parking in any portion of any street.

The city traffic engineer may also establish the hours and days when such time
limits shall be effective. The city traffic engineer shall provide for the posting of
signs giving notice of such time limits and special restrictions. In the absence of
signs giving notice of such special restrictions, the general provisions of the traffic
code shall govern.

B. Hours and Days Excepted. Time limits on parking imposed pursuant to the
preceding subsection shall be applicable between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 6:00
p.m. daily except city-recognized holidays.


                                  Chapter 19.03
                                   DEFINITIONS

19.03.010     Definitions.

Bicycle Lane. Any portion of the roadway which has been designated by traffic-
control devices for preferential or exclusive use by bicycles.

Block Face. One side of a block between road intersections.

Camper. Any vehicle either manufactured, modified, or used to facilitate human
habitation or temporary lodging.

Electric Vehicle. Any vehicle that operates, either partially or exclusively, on
electrical energy from an off-board source, that is stored on-board for motive
purpose. Electric vehicle includes any battery electric vehicle and any plug-in
hybrid electric vehicle.




                                                                                        Page 39 of 578
Highway. Every way, lane, road, alley, street, boulevard, highway, parking area,
and every way or place in the city of Vancouver adopted to and fitted for travel,
that is in common use by the public with the consent, implied or express, of the
owner.

Payment Collection Device. Any mechanical or electronic device or platform that
requires collects payment in exchange for authorized parking in designated,
public parking areas. A parking meter is placed immediately adjacent to an
individual, parking space, and the parking meter reveals the remaining amount of
time for authorized parking.

Residential Area. Those areas of the city which have been designated as
residential districts for purposes of the Zoning Code (Title 20 of this code).

Trailer. Any vehicle without motive power designed for carrying persons or
property on its own structure and to be drawn by a vehicle with motor power.
The term trailer includes trailer coach, semitrailer, boat trailer, or utility trailer.



                                   Chapter 19.04
                         PARKING ADMINISTRATION

19.04.010      Parking type and time stays in established parking meter zones.

Authorized parking and maximum time stays established. It is hereby established
that metered parking that is regulated by a payment collection device, permit,
signed, and /or other types of parking as approved by council are hereby
authorized in established parking meter zones. There is hereby established a
maximum parking time stay of ten (10) hours in established parking meter zones
between the hours of 8AM to 6PM, except on city recognized holidays.




                                                                                          Page 40 of 578
The City Manager, or his/her their designee, with advice from the Parking
Advisory Committee, is hereby delegated the administrative authority to
determine:

A. Which of the authorized types of parking shall be used in established parking
meter zones;

B. What time stays are appropriate for both meters parking spaces regulated by
a payment collection device and signed parking within the established parking
meter zones, not to exceed a maximum of ten (10) hours between the hours of
8AM to 6PM, except on city recognized holidays,; and

C. Rules and regulations regarding the administrative change of the type of
authorized parking allowed and the reduction of the maximum time stay in
established parking meter zones.

The City Manager, or his/her their designee, with advice from the Parking
Advisory Committee, may administratively change the type of authorized parking
to be used in an established parking meter zone and may reduce metered time
limits for parking in spaces regulated by a payment collection device or signed
parking time stays in established parking meter zones to less than ten (10) hours
between the hours of 8AM to 6PM, except on city recognized holidays for an area
not to exceed a contiguous 200 feet of parking stalls upon consideration of any of
the following factors:

   1. The nature and character of the land use in the area including any recent
   changes;

   2. The market conditions in the Portland-Vancouver area including any
   recent changes;

   3. Discussions with property owners on the affected block face;




                                                                                  Page 41 of 578
   4. Occupancy rates in the area including any recent changes; and/or

   5. Any other relevant factors.

   The City Manager, or his/her their designee, shall report to the City Council
   regarding changes in authorized parking and parking time stays in established
   parking meter zones as requested by the City Council, but in any event, shall
   report at least once every year.

The city council may, by resolution, enlarge or reduce the parking meter zones.

19.04.030    Parking meter Payment collection device installation.

The city traffic engineer and/or parking division is authorized to install and

                                 Chapter 19.06
         MUNICIPAL LOT AT EVERGREEN AND BROADWAY

19.06.010    Operation – Availability.

The municipal parking lot shall be operated by the City of Vancouver unless and
until a contract is entered into providing for private operation thereof. It shall be
open and available to public use every day of the year and for all hours of the day
and night except for such time during early morning hours as it is necessary to
close the lot for cleaning.

19.06.020    General use.

Use of the municipal parking lot at Evergreen and Broadway shall be free of any
charge except as here provided.

19.06.030    Rates.

Use of seventeen spaces shall be limited to one hour of use and thirty-five spaces
shall be limited to two hours of use; provided, not to exceed eleven spaces shall
be available for long term permit use under the criteria herein provided and upon
payment of the monthly fee of a maximum rate of two hundred dollars ($200.00),
which may be reduced administratively by the city manager or his/her their
designee pursuant to the guidelines set forth in section 19.11.040. The city
manager, or his/her their designee, shall report to the city council from time to
time as requested by the city council, but in any event, shall report at least once
every year regarding these parking rates.




                                                                                    Page 47 of 578
19.06.040    Long-term use.

As to the spaces to be available for long-term use, it is anticipated that more
applications may be made than there will be spaces available. Accordingly, city
staff is directed to give preference to persons who apply for a monthly permit and
who manage a store, shop, office or restaurant immediately adjacent to the lot
and who frequently need to be "in and out" of their places of business.

19.06.050    Permits.

Permits shall be issued in the name of the store, shop, office, or restaurant and
may be used by anyone employed there, but only one shall be issued for each
such business unless other such permits remain available. If other monthly
permits remain available, they may be issued on a first come first served basis, or
if there still are unused spaces the spaces may be temporarily used for two hour
parking.

19.06.060    Applications for permits.

Applications for permits under this section shall be made to the city division of
economic development on forms to be prepared by it. Applications may be made
at any time and be accompanied by the monthly fee. The permits issued shall be
monthly permits and the fee must be paid by the 20th of the month preceding
use.

19.06.070    Signs.

Signs shall be posted as necessary to effectuate this section.

19.06.080    Disposition of revenues.

Revenues from parking permits shall be paid to the parking operations fund.

19.06.090    Penalties and violations.




                                                                                    Page 48 of 578
All of the provisions, violations, and penalties contained in VMC 19.07.030, and
VMC 19.07.050 shall apply to chapter 19.06.



                                 Chapter 19.07
               OTHER MUNICIPAL LOTS AND FACILITIES

19.07.010     Designated – Exemption.

All public parking lots and facilities owned, or leased, and/or operated by the city,
except for the municipal parking lot at Broadway and Evergreen which is
governed by ordinances codified in chapter 19.06 of this code, shall be covered by
and subject to this chapter.

19.07.020    Rates and regulations.

The city council City Manager or their designee is authorized to provide for short-
term, long-term, all-day or monthly use of such off-street public parking facilities
as demand indicates and as necessary for the public safety, and to set rates for
such use.

A. The rates in section 19.11.040 shall apply to all public parking lots and
facilities owned, leased, and/or operated by the city of Vancouver. Parking rates
for such facilities may be reduced administratively by the city manager or his/her
their designee, pursuant to the guidelines in section 19.11.040.

B. The City Manager or his/her their designee is authorized to establish
reasonable regulations as to the use of such parking facilities and provide
notification of such regulations either by posting signs in appropriate facilities or
by providing written notice to authorized users.




                                                                                    Page 49 of 578
C. Notwithstanding other provisions within this Title, revenue generated by off-
street parking lots that primarily support city facilities, such as City Hall, Pearson
Field Airport, and City Parks, may be remitted to the fund associated with said
facility and may be spent without restriction. Provided, the parking division shall
be reimbursed for any costs incurred by the parking division related to
maintenance, enforcement, revenue collection, or any other activities performed
at such off street lots.

19.07.030      Violations – Penalties.

A. Violation of this section shall be an infraction. It shall be unlawful to park a
vehicle in any of the facilities except after payment of applicable fees, and except
in compliance with applicable permit, parking meter payment collection device,
and/or sign requirements. Notice of violation of the provisions of this section shall
be given in writing on a form provided by the department of finance and shall
instruct the owner or operator of the vehicle to pay the penalty imposed in this
section. The notice shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on the vehicle parked
in violation of this chapter or other ordinance. Penalties for overtime violation
shall be as set forth in chapter 19.13.

B. Penalties for violations of other parking lot regulations shall be as set forth in
chapter 19.13.

In addition to penalties imposed by this section, law enforcement officers,
including fully and specially commissioned officers, and persons employed to
administer this chapter or their assigns are authorized to cause the removal and
impoundment of vehicles violating this chapter or such regulations. Costs of
impounding and storing shall be paid by the vehicle's owner or his/her their
designee. Signs advising of the requirements of this section shall be posted in
each affected parking lot or facility.




                                                                                      Page 50 of 578
19.07.040    Disposition of revenues.

Fees and penalties received under this chapter shall be paid into the parking
operations fund.

19.07.050    Driving violation.

Driving violations in any such public parking facility shall be prosecuted or
administered under the city's traffic code and all such parking facilities are
specifically established as highways as defined in VMC 9.04.440 for the purpose of
enforcement of traffic regulations.

            SPECIAL PARKING USES OF THE RIGHT OF WAY

19.10.010     Carpool parking.

Persons who are issued or who have been issued a carpool space permit under

19.10.040    Parking for persons with disabilities.

Persons who are issued or who have been issued a parking permit for persons
with disabilities under state law may park their vehicles in compliance with
regulations thereof.

Provided, however, free parking is limited to a maximum of four hours on any one
day in the following situations: (1) Vehicles displaying a special parking placard for
persons with disabilities or special parking license plate for persons with
disabilities in nonreserved, on-street parking spaces; (2) vehicles displaying a
special parking placard for persons with disabilities or special parking license plate
for persons with disabilities in nonmetered, on-street parking places reserved for
persons with physical disabilities. These time restrictions shall be clearly posted
and shall apply between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., except on city-
recognized holidays, in the following geographical area: Commencing at the
intersection of E Fourth Plain Boulevard and Lincoln Street, then east along Fourth
Plain Boulevard to Interstate 5, then south along Interstate 5 to the Columbia
River, then west along the Columbia River to the alignment of Lincoln Street if it
were extended south of 8th Street, and then north following the alignment of
Lincoln Street to Fourth Plain Boulevard to the point of beginning.

19.10.050     Long-term permit parking.

A. Long-term permit parking is allowed in those parts of the city marked for
permit parking. In those parts of the city which are marked for "permit parking"
parking by permit, signs shall be installed to limit allow for the parking to of
vehicles for which a parking permit has been issued under the provisions of this




                                                                                      Page 58 of 578
section and section 19.04.070, and it shall be a violation of this section for anyone
to park in any such a parking permit only space unless a parking permit for such
vehicle has been secured under the provisions of section 19.04.070. Physical and
unless such permits must be is properly displayed in or on such vehicle so that it is
readily observable by parking control officers in accordance with the permit
agreement.

B. Any person who violates or fails to comply with the provisions of this section
shall be subject to the penalties provided for in section 19.13.050.

19.10.060    Media parking permits.

A. Any operator of a newspaper, radio station or television station may apply to
the parking department of public works and be issued one or more media parking
permits upon payment of a fee of $50.00 per permit. The media parking permit
shall be issued on a calendar year basis and shall expire on December 31st of the
year of issue; for permits issued in 1992 the fee shall be prorated based on the
remaining full months in the year.

B. The permittee may use it on any vehicle and shall display the permit to be
easily visible through the windshield. When properly thus displayed the vehicle
may be parked at a parking meter without payment of a parking fee.

C. The permit is to be used to attend specific news events. The intent of such
permit is to avoid the need for the journalist to leave a news event to insert coins
in a parking meter pay for parking; the permit is not intended to be used while
attending routine meetings. The permit shall not allow the permittee to park in
violation of any other parking regulation.

19.10.070    Truck, trailer, and motor home residential street permits.




                                                                                   Page 59 of 578
A. The city manager, or his/her their designee, may issue special written permits
allowing the location of a motor home, trailer, or travel trailer, or camper on a
street or public right of way for repair or sleeping purposes only, which permit
shall allow the owner the right to park such vehicle at the location described in
the permit for a period of seven days which may be renewable for a period up to
seven (7) additional days in any one calendar year and shall be issued without fee.
Approval of location is partly contingent upon written permission of the abutting
property owner. Special permits may only be issued for the following reasons: (1)
Emergency repair requiring more than eight hours; (2) Guest visiting a resident of
the city. Said permit must be posted and visible from the exterior of the motor
home, trailer, or travel trailer, or camper.

B. The city manager, or his/her their designee, is authorized to promulgate rules
and regulations regarding the implementation and enforcement of this ordinance.

C. The city manager, or his/her their designee, is authorized to revoke a permit
that has been issued if he or she they finds lack of compliance with any
requirement of subsection (iA), above, or of the rules and regulations
promulgated under subsection (iiB), above, or of any ordinance or statute.

D. Any person who is denied a permit, or had his/her their permit revoked, may
appeal the denial/revocation to a hearings examiner appointed by the city
manager, or his/her their designee the head of the issuing department. Notice of
appeal must be in writing, and filed with the city clerk within seven (7) working
days from the date of the denial.

19.10.080    Law enforcement parking permits.

A. Upon payment of a fee to the Parking Fund, the City manager or designee
may issue law enforcement parking permits to a chief of police or county sheriff
for the purpose of authorizing official unmarked law enforcement vehicles on




                                                                                    Page 60 of 578
official business to park at metered parking spaces without payment to the meter
for periods longer than the posted time limit.

B. In the event that the City manager or designee has elected to issue permits to
a chief of police or county sheriff, the chief of police or county sheriff may issue
the law enforcement parking permits to law enforcement personnel within his or
her their agency as the chief of police or county sheriff deems appropriate.

C. The permit shall be in or on such vehicle so that it is readily observable by
parking services officers.

D. Permits shall expire at the end of each calendar year. The chief of police,
county sheriff or designee shall renew existing permits or obtain new permits
from the City manager or designee within five (5) working days of the expiration
date.

E. The permit fee shall be established based on recovery of lost parking meter
revenue and expenses incurred to provide law enforcement parking permit
services.

F. The chief of police, county sheriff or designee shall cancel any permit that is
no longer needed. The chief of police, county sheriff or designee shall retrieve and
cancel any permit that is not properly used.

19.10.090     On-street parking reservations.

A. Parking space (s) may be reserved for reasons including but not limited to: (a)
special access to a facility; (b) building or street construction; (c) remodeling; (d)
special events; or (e) moving subject to the requirements and procedures of this
section.

B. Meter hoods Parking Reservations shall be used to secure on-street metered
parking spaces. Reservations may be made for the following purposes: (a) to




                                                                                       Page 61 of 578
accommodate large moving trucks; (b) to facilitate construction on property
adjacent to the street; to accommodate events; (c) to prohibit parking for block
parties, races, or parades; or (d) for a purpose determined by the Parking
Manager to be in the interest of the City. All uses require payment as provided for
in Section E. If reservations are to be made for other than the herein purposes, a
street use permit must also be obtained as provided for in VMC Chapter 11.60

C. Signs stating “no parking” shall be used to secure reserved parking spaces in
areas where there are no parking meters and that fall within the Parking Advisory
Committee’s boundary as identified in VMC 2.63.060. Reservations may be made
for the following purposes: (a) to accommodate large moving trucks; (b) to
facilitate construction on property adjacent to the street; to accommodate events;
(c) to prohibit parking for block parties, races, or parades; or (d) for a purpose
determined by the Parking Manager to be in the interest of the City. All uses
require payment as provided for in Section E. If reservations are to be made for
other than the herein purposes, a street use permit must also be obtained as
provided for in VMC Chapter 11.60.

D. Arrangements to reserve an on-street space (s) shall be made by contacting
the City’s Parking Services Division.

   1. Applications must be submitted at least 21 days before the reservation is
   needed. For good cause shown, this period may be reduced by the Parking
   Manager.

   2. The applicant must provide dates and times when the reservation is to
   start and end and the specific location and number of spaces needed.

   3. City departments and other governmental entities are required to follow
   the same policy and procedures for reserving space (s) as other applicants.




                                                                                     Page 62 of 578
4. No use of the reserved spaces may be made unless meters are hooded or
“no parking” signs are correctly displayed.

5. City Contractors, City departments and other governmental entities shall
not be required to pay for reserving spaces under the following
circumstances:

   a. Emergencies;

   b. Planned projects including but not limited to sidewalk repair, right of
   way and street maintenance; or

   c. Reconstruction of a street.

6. Parking tickets incurred before and after reservation dates or by use of the
reserved space not in compliance with City guidelines are the responsibility of
the vehicle owner as provided for by law.

7. Reserving Metered or Non-metered parking space (s) shall not be used
solely for employee parking.

8. The Parking Manager reserves the right to limit the number of parking
spaces reserved by an applicant.

9. If an applicant fails to comply with state law or the requirements of this
code section or requirements of the permit reservation agreement, the
reservation may be cancelled and the hood (s) or sign (s) removed without
notice.

10. No meter payment collection devices or no-parking signs may be
tampered with, moved, or removed by an applicant without permission from
the Parking Manager.




                                                                                Page 63 of 578
   11. Applicants exempted from obtaining a street use permit shall submit a
   completed Parking Stall Closure Acknowledgement form with the reservation
   application and complete the required process prior to use.

   12. Meter hoods or temporary "No parking" signs shall be placed 24 hours in
   advance of the start of the applicant’s reservation.

E. Fees.

   1. Metered Zones. A daily rate per-metered space-per-24 hour day fee, a fifty
   dollar ($50) refundable per meter hood deposit, and a non-refundable forty-
   five dollar ($45) per-application administrative fee will be charged for
   reservations. Fees will not be prorated for hourly or half-day services.

   2. Non-Metered Zones. A daily rate per-space-per-24 hour day fee plus and a
   non-refundable forty-five dollar ($45) per-application administrative fee will
   be charged for reservations. Fees will not be prorated for hourly or half-day
   services.

   3. Special Events. A daily rate per-space-per-24 hour day fee, a fifty dollar
   ($50) refundable per meter hood deposit (if applicable), and a non-refundable
   forty-five dollar ($45) per-application administrative fee will be charged for
   reservations. Fees will not be prorated for hourly or half-day services.

   4. All fees and deposits shall be paid in advance.

   5. The applicant is responsible for additional fees if use of the reserved spaces
   continues after the end date.

F. Meter Hoods No Parking Signs.

   1. Once the meter reservation expires, the applicant shall return the hoods
   "no parking" signs in as good a condition as they were received (normal wear




                                                                                    Page 64 of 578
   excepted), and shall thereupon be refunded the deposit fee. If the applicant
   requires an extension for their reservation, the applicant shall pay the
   additional daily rate per-meter-per-24 hour day fee for the extended period,
   but shall not be liable for any additional deposit.

   2. If any meter reservation under this section expires and the meter hoods
   have not been refunded and an extension has not been granted under
   subsection F, all rights to use such hoods "no parking" signs shall lapse and
   they shall be recovered and the deposit fee shall be deemed forfeited to the
   City. It shall be a violation of this section for anyone to lend or rent any meter
   hoods "no parking" signs issued under a reservation granted under this
   section to any other person or contractor or to use any such hood sign at a
   location other than that specified in such permit. Any person found to be
   engaged in such activity shall forfeit the right to a refund of the deposit fees.



                                Chapter 19.11
                        PARKING RATES AND FEES

19.11.010     Parking rates.

A. On Street Parking. The city manager, or his or her their designee, shall set
rates for the use of parking pay stations parking spaces regulated by a payment
collection device for on street parking in parking meter zones, according to the
rates applicable to parking meters provisions contained in section 19.11.030.

B. Off Street Parking. The city manager, or his or her their designee, shall set
rates for the use of parking pay stations parking spaces regulated by a payment
collection device for off street parking in city owned, leased, and/or operated




                                                                                   Page 65 of 578
parking lots and facilities, according to the provisions contained in section
19.11.040.

19.11.020    Parking meter modification.

All one or two hour meters in all zones shall be modified so that the user can by
operating the lever thereon have the first fifteen minutes free of charge.

19.11.030    Parking meter fees designated Rates for on street parking.

A. Between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. daily except days being
celebrated as any city-recognized holiday, the operator of a vehicle, upon
entering any metered parking space regulated by a payment collection device,
shall immediately deposit, in the proper adjacent parking meter, coins utilize the
appropriate payment collection device to pay for parking in an amount totaling no
more than $3.50 per hour as shown on the meter by the payment collection
device, and shall put the meter in operation. (In some short-term meters a
portion of the hour is available free by turning the dial of the meter.) If the vehicle
remains parked in the parking space beyond the legal parking time which is
designated by a sign or signal on the parking meter, such vehicle shall be
considered as parked overtime. In zones where parking is limited to 15 minutes or
less per use, the meter fee shall be no more than $0.70 per quarter hour. In zones
where parking is limited to 30 minutes or less per use, the meter fee shall be no
more than $1.30 per half hour. In zones where parking is limited to two hours or
less per use, the meter fee shall be no more than $3.50 per hour. In zones where
parking is permitted for longer than two hours per use, the meter fee shall be no
more than $3.50 per hour. Where established parking periods are shorter than 1-
hour, rates shall be a proportional fraction of the hourly rate.

The parking meter hourly fee rate may be reduced administratively by the city
manager or his/her their designee in accordance with the provisions of VMC




                                                                                    Page 66 of 578
19.11.040. The city manager, or his/her their designee, shall report to the city
council from time to time as requested by the city council, but in any event, shall
report at least once every year regarding these parking rates.

B. The department of public works shall cause for there to be installed on each
parking meter a suitable plate informing of the hours and days in which such
metered parking regulations are enforced.

19.11.040    Rates in public off-street facilities.

There is hereby established a maximum daily parking rate of $25.00, a maximum
monthly parking rate of $200.00, and a maximum event rate of $25.00 per event
stay in parking lots or facilities owned, leased, and/or operated by the city. These
rates may be reduced administratively by the city manager, or his/her their
designee, pursuant to the guidelines below:

A. Any citizen 62 years of age, or older, may receive a “senior citizen discount” in
an amount to be determined by the city manager or his/her their designee, but in
no event should the discount exceed 20 percent;

B. The parking rates may be changed to an amount to reach the desired
occupancy rate in each municipal lot or facility;

C. The parking rates may be adjusted annually pursuant to the methodology set
forth in VMC 3.08.100;

D. The parking rates may be changed to an amount to reach desired occupancy
rates at parking meters for on street parking;

E. The parking rates may be changed to reflect market conditions in the
Portland-Vancouver area;




                                                                                   Page 67 of 578
F. The parking rates may be changed to accommodate specific site
characteristics and seasonal events;

G. The parking rates may be changed to reflect the parking conditions, including,
but not limited to, covered vs. uncovered parking, and reserved vs. non-reserved.

The city manager, or his/her their designee, is authorized to promulgate rules and
regulations regarding the administrative reduction of the maximum parking rates.
The city manager, or his/her their designee, shall report to the city council from
time to time as requested by the city council, but in any event, shall report at
least once every year regarding these parking rates.

19.11.060    Zone 3 – Parking meter fees.

Parking meter fees are established for the parking meters as follows: between the
hours of 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. daily except days being celebrated as any city-
recognized holiday, no more than $3.50 per hour of use for the one- and two-
hour meters; no more than $3.50 per hour of use for the 10-hour meters. These
parking meter fees may be reduced administratively by the city manager or
his/her designee, pursuant to the guidelines referred to in VMC 19.11.040. The
city manager, or his/her designee, shall report to the city council from time to
time as requested by the city council, but in any event, shall report at least once
every year regarding these parking rates.



                                 Chapter 19.12
                          PARKING PROHIBITIONS

19.12.010     General parking prohibitions – Exceptions.




                                                                                     Page 68 of 578
Notwithstanding the provisions of RCW 46.61.570(b)(ii), the city traffic engineer
may provide for parking within fifteen feet of any fire hydrant so long as access to
any fire hydrant is not blocked by property properly parked vehicles.

19.12.020     Moving to evade, identification, and penalty.

A. Moving to Evade. It is unlawful for any person to move a vehicle from one
parking space location to any other parking space location on the same block face
or the block face across the street from where the vehicle was previously parked,
or to move a vehicle from one parking space to another space within the same
off-street facility, for the purpose of evading time limitations on parking. There
shall be a rebuttable presumption that any person employed or working in Zone
1, 1A, 2 or 3 who moves a vehicle from one parking space to another and then
returns directly or indirectly to work has moved such vehicle for the purpose of
evading time limitations on parking.

B. Chalk Mark Identifications. In checking for overtime parking, police officers,
community service inspectors, and parking enforcement officers are authorized to
use chalk marks on the tires of parked vehicles, or any other identifying mark that
does not deface the vehicle, and it is unlawful for any person to erase or
obliterate such mark for the purpose of interfering with such checking for
overtime parking.

C. Penalty. Notice of any such violation shall be given in accordance with the
traffic code and rules adopted pursuant thereto. Penalties for violation shall be as
set forth in chapter 19.13.

19.12.030 Street Sweeping Parking Limitations.

A. No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle upon any highway in the City of
Vancouver that will interfere with the reasonable operation of public works




                                                                                     Page 69 of 578
department sweeping or maintenance after public notice has been given by the
City by way of permanent signs or temporary signs placed 24 hours in advance.

Any vehicle parked in violation of this section may be cited or removed in
accordance with RCW 46.55.

19.12.040       Parking on public property.

No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle on any city park, playground or
recreation area, or on any other city-owned property if prohibited by resolution
of the city council. The city council, by resolution, is authorized, with reference to
the aforementioned property, to prohibit parking on all or any portion of the
property and may further provide that such prohibition shall be effective at all
times or only at certain specified times. The city council shall provide for the
posting of signs giving notice of such prohibited parking and the hours thereof. No
person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle in any such sign posted zone during the
periods of time so specified.

Any person who shall violate or fail to comply with the provisions of this section,
after parking restrictions or prohibitions have been lawfully established, shall be
subject to the penalties provided for in the traffic code. The vehicle shall be
subject to removal as provided for in the tow provisions of the traffic code.

19.12.050       Backed-in parking.

A. It shall be unlawful to park any vehicle in any parking space in a backed-in
position in any of the several public parking facilities operated by the city under
RCW Chapters 35.86 or 35.86A.

B. Staff shall post such signs as seem necessary to effectuate subsection (A) of
this section.




                                                                                    Page 70 of 578
C. Anyone violating subsection (A) of this section shall be issued a citation, which
may be filed in court consistent with statutes and court rules. Penalties for
violation shall be as set forth in chapter 19.13.

19.12.060    Parking while loading and unloading.

A. Passenger Vehicles. Passenger vehicles used for hauling commodities property
or persons shall, when loading or unloading such commodities property or
persons, be stopped or parked parallel or diagonally to the curb as required by
the type of parking indicated by markings or sign and shall not be backed to the
curb unless otherwise directed by signage, striping or other traffic control device.

B. Commercial Vehicles. Except when actually actively engaged in loading or
unloading some commodity, no commercial vehicle shall stand backed to the curb
at any time. All loading and unloading shall be continuous and shall be completed
as rapidly as possible. All commercial vehicles backed to the curb within a
business district for the purpose of loading and unloading commodities shall
stand at right angles to the curb with the rear wheels against the curb or street
line in cases where the length of the vehicle will permit such parking without
blocking a substantial portion of the street; otherwise, the vehicle shall be parked
parallel to the curb unless otherwise directed by signage, striping or other traffic
control device, or at an angle with the curb with the right rear wheel against the
curb or street line; provided, however, that no vehicle shall be backed against or
parked at the curb or street line at any place within a business district so that the
foremost part of such vehicle extends out into the street to a point nearer than
six feet from the center of the street, unless a permit for such parking has been
obtained from the chief of police.

C. Long and Heavy Vehicles. No vehicle or combination of vehicles of greater
length than thirty feet shall be stopped or parked for loading and unloading




                                                                                    Page 71 of 578
purposes on any street within a business district of the city of Vancouver, except
upon written permit from the chief of police.

19.12.070       Parking in alleys.

No vehicle shall be parked in any alley, except when actually actively engaged in
loading or unloading some commodity or when there is a driver at the wheel
capable of moving the same.

19.12.080        Truck, trailer, and motor home parking on residential streets.

A. No person shall park or leave standing on any street or public right of way of
any residential area of the city, any of the following:

1. A truck with a gross weight capacity in excess of nine thousand pounds;
commercial vehicle with any of the following characteristics unless loading,
unloading, or actively engaged in commerce:

      a. A registered gross weight capacity in excess of nine thousand pounds;

      b. A height in excess of 10 feet;

      c. A width in excess of 7.5 feet; or

      d. A length in excess of 25 feet.

2. A trailer;

3. A travel trailer;

4. A motor home.;

5. A camper.

B. The provisions of this section shall not apply to any vehicle which is parked or
left standing expressly for the purpose of loading or unloading. For the purposes




                                                                                  Page 72 of 578
of this section, a reasonable amount of time on any day or successive days shall
be allowed for loading and unloading, the amount of which time is to be
determined according to the nature and extent of the loading and unloading
operation.

C. Impound authorized. For the purposes of this section, in addition to, or in lieu
of, issuing a citation, law enforcement officers, including fully and specially
commissioned officers, are authorized to impound pursuant to the procedures set
forth in R.C.W. 46.55.085.

19.12.090    Obstructing Traffic.

No person shall park any vehicle upon any highway in a manner which obstructs
or otherwise interferes with vehicular traffic, or bicycle traffic, or safe pedestrian
traffic upon the traveled portions of the roadway, and bicycle lane, and sidewalk.

19.12.100    Prolonged Parking.

A. No vehicles shall remain parked on a highway longer than 24 hours without a
valid permit. Vehicles parked longer than 24 hours may be issued a parking
citation.

B. In addition to, or in lieu of, issuing a citation, a law enforcement officer may
take custody of a vehicle that is in violation of this section and provide for the
vehicle’s removal to a place of safety, subject to the following requirements:

    1. A law enforcement officer discovering an unauthorized vehicle left upon a
    highway shall visibly mark the vehicle and attach to the vehicle a readily
    visible notification tag. The tag shall contain the following information:

        a. The date and time the tag was attached;

        b. The identity of the officer.




                                                                                      Page 73 of 578
      c. A statement that if the vehicle is not removed within twenty-four
      hours from the time the tag is attached, the officer may issue a parking
      citation and the vehicle may be taken into custody and stored at the
      owner’s expense;

      d. A statement that if the vehicle is not redeemed as provided in RCW
      46.55.120, the registered owner will have committed the traffic infraction
      of littering – abandoned vehicle; and

       e. The address and telephone number where additional information may
       be obtained.

   2. If the vehicle has current Washington registration plates, the officer shall
   check the records to learn the identity of the last owner of record. The officer
   or his or her their department shall make a reasonable effort to contact the
   owner by telephone in order to give the owner the information on the
   notification tag.

   3. If the vehicle is not removed within twenty-four hours from the time the
   notification sticker tag is attached, the law enforcement officer may take
   custody of the vehicle and provide for the vehicle's removal to a place of
   safety. A vehicle that does not pose a safety hazard may remain on the
   roadside for more than twenty-four hours if the owner or operator is unable
   to remove it from the place where it is located and so notifies law
   enforcement officials and requests assistance.

   4. For the purposes of this section a place of safety includes the business
   location of a registered tow truck operator.

19.12.110    Expired Tabs Improper Vehicle License Plate.




                                                                                  Page 74 of 578
A. No person shall stop, stand or park any vehicle on any street or alley, or in any
garage, parking area or other property owned, leased, and/or operated by the
City, without first having displayed current and proper vehicle license plates
thereon as provided in Chapter 46.16A RCW. The vehicle license plates shall be
attached conspicuously in the manner required by RCW 46.16A.200.

B. Any person who shall violate or fail to comply with the provisions of this
section shall be subject to the penalties provided for in the parking code.



                                 Chapter 19.13
                           PARKING VIOLATIONS

19.13.010     Compliance required – Pay stations Payment collection devices.

A. Compliance with Instructions and Limitations of Use. Every person who parks a
vehicle in an area regulated by a parking pay station payment collection device is
required to comply with the instructions for use, including, but not limited to,
applicable time limits, proper payment, and proper proof and display of payment
identification of such vehicle for which parking has been paid.

B. Permits. Any valid, city issued permit that exempts an individual from paying
parking meter fees shall also exempt that individual from the payments required
by parking pay stations; a payment collection device shall do so provided, that the
holder of any authorized such permit complies with the permit’s conditions.

19.13.020    Violation notices – Parking meters.

The parking prohibitions and restrictions provided in sections 19.04.010,
19.04.030, 19.11.030, of this code are designated traffic infractions relating to the
following:



                                                                                   Page 75 of 578
A. Expired Meter – No person shall permit a vehicle within his/her control to be
parked in any parking meter space during the restricted and regulated time
applicable to the parking meter zone in which such meter is located while the
parking meter for such space indicates by signal that the lawful parking time in
such space has expired. Penalties for such expired meter parking violations in all
metered zones shall be as set forth in chapter 19.13.

B. Overtime Parking – No person shall park a vehicle in any parking meter space
for a consecutive period of time longer than that limited period of time for which
parking is lawfully permitted in the parking meter zone in which such meter is
located, irrespective of the number or amounts of the coins deposited in such
meter. Penalties for such overtime parking violations in all metered and
unmetered zones shall be as set forth in chapter 19.13.

19.13.030     Violations – Pay stations Payment collection devices.

A. It shall be a violation of this chapter to fail to obey the instructions
requirements for use of any parking space(s) regulated by a parking pay station
payment collection device, including, but not limited to:

   1. Overtime Parking. Parking in any area, regulated by signage, parking meter
   or parking pay station a payment collection device, for longer than allowed by
   the applicable limit a consecutive period of time longer than that limited
   period of time for which parking is lawfully permitted; and

   2. Expired Proof of Payment. Displaying Expired proof of payment on for any
   vehicle parked in a parking space, regulated by a parking meter or parking pay
   station payment collection device; and

   3. No Proof of Payment. Failing to properly display proof of payment on
   immediately utilize the appropriate payment collection device to pay for any




                                                                                   Page 76 of 578
   vehicle parked in a parking space, regulated by a parking meter or parking pay
   station payment collection device.

   4. Improper Payment. Failing to properly identify any vehicle parked in a
   parking space regulated by a payment collection device.

B. Classification of Infraction. Every violation of this chapter constitutes an
infraction.

C. Notice of infraction. A notice of infraction for a violation of this chapter shall
be issued and processed according to the procedures contained in chapter 19.13,
Parking Violations.

D. Use of Fines. All fines collected, pursuant to this chapter, shall be deposited
and used according to the limitations contained in section 19.04.080, Parking
operations funds.

19.13.050     Parking fines and penalties.

Parking fines associated with parking violations related to meter violations,
overtime violations, violations involving parking for persons with disabilities,
parking lot violations and other violations shall be as follows:

A. Expired Meter. Penalties for expired meter violations shall be $25.00 for each
violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $50.00 for each
violation if paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.

BA. Paystation Payment Collection Device Violation. Penalties for paystation
payment collection device violations shall be $25.00 $40.00 for each violation if
paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $50.00 $65.00 for each violation
if paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.




                                                                                     Page 77 of 578
CB. Overtime Violation Parking. Penalties for overtime parking shall be $30.00
$40.00 for each violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and
$25.00 $65.00 for each violation if paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.

DC. Improper Parking. Penalties for improper parking shall be $35.00 $40.00 for
each violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $25.00 $65.00 if
paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.

ED. Prohibited Parking. Penalties for prohibited parking shall be $40.00 $65.00
for each violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $65.00
$90.00 if paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.

FE. Moving to Evade. Penalties for moving to evade violations shall be $35.00
$40.00 for each violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and
$60.00 $65.00 if paid or postmarked after 30 calendar days.

GF. Violations involving parking for persons with disabilities. Fines, penalties, and
assessments for violations of RCW 46.19.050 regarding special parking for persons
with disabilities shall be provided in RCW 46.19.050.

HG. Expired Tabs Improper Vehicle License Plate. Penalties for expired tabs
improper vehicle license plate violations shall be $50.00 $65.00 for each violation
if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $75.00 $90.00 if paid or
postmarked after 30 calendar days.

IH. Permit Parking Violations. Penalties for permit parking area violations on a
highway, municipal parking lot, or public parking lot shall be $25.00 $40.00 for
each violation if paid or postmarked within 30 calendar days, and $50.00 $65.00 if
paid or postmarked after 30 days.

                                 Chapter 19.14
              PARKING VIOLATIONS – ADMINISTRATION

19.14.010     Notices.

A. Notices of parking violations shall be given in accordance with the traffic code.

B. Unless otherwise provided for, the penalty for violating the parking provisions
of the traffic code shall be as set forth in section 19.12 19.13. In addition to the
penalties imposed by this chapter, law enforcement officers, including fully and
specially commissioned officers, are authorized to cause the removal and
impoundment of vehicles violating such enumerated provisions. Costs of
impoundment and storage shall be paid by the vehicle's owner.

The penalties above provided and the authority to impound for violation shall also
apply to vehicles parked in:

   1. Bus zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.010;

   2. Taxi zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.040;

   3. Loading zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.050 and VMC 9.60.060;

   4. Theater zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.070 and VMC 9.60.080;

   5. Funeral zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.090 and VMC 9.60.100;

   6. Construction zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.110;




                                                                                       Page 84 of 578
   7. City use zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.120;

   8. County use zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.130;

   9. Tourist use zones established pursuant to VMC 9.60.140;

   10. The parking prohibitions and restrictions provided in section 19.12.010.

19.14.020    Presumption of ownership.

It shall be a rebuttable presumption that each vehicle ticketed for a violation of
the ordinance provisions enumerated in section 19.14.010 is in fact owned by its
registered owner and that such owner is responsible for the ticket so issued.

19.14.030    Authority to issue notices.

Parking enforcement officers shall be special police officers under VMC 2.20.030.
All City of Vancouver parking enforcement officers, currently employed or
employed hereafter, or any employee of the city assigned by the city manager or
his or her their designee to perform the duties of a parking enforcement officer,
are authorized to issue notices of traffic infraction for violations of city parking
ordinances. Such notices also may be issued by any police officer. All such notices
shall be issued in accordance with procedures established by RCW Chapter 46.63,
Supreme Court and local court rules, and applicable city ordinances.

19.14.040    Processing Infraction – Duty.

The duties and responsibilities of the city Department of Finance shall include the
processing of parking infractions involving alleged violations of city parking
ordinances in accordance with Clark County District Court Order entered
December 16, 1980. Processing of such infractions shall be in accordance with
procedures established by said court order, RCW Chapter 46.63, applicable
Supreme Court and local court rules, and related city ordinances. For the purpose




                                                                                       Page 85 of 578
of processing infractions, the department of finance is designated a violations
bureau, as established by the order entered on December 16, 1980.

19.14.050    Processing Infractions – Costs.

Employees of the department of finance who are assigned duties relating to the
processing of traffic infractions shall be city employees and the costs of the
operation of the violations bureau established by Clark County District Court
Order entered December 16, 1980 shall be paid by the city from the fund to which
said expenses are properly chargeable.

19.14.060     Disposition of traffic fines and forfeitures.

All fines and forfeitures collected for violation of the traffic code, unless herein
otherwise provided for, shall be paid into the general fund of the city; provided,
those monies collected by the court or city as assessments per statutes for
disbursement to other governmental agencies shall be so disbursed.

Message

      I’m strongly opposed to raising our city’s income tax to increase police funding. The PD can’t fill the roles
      that are ALREADY funded (see current vacancies). We already don’t have enough public defenders to
      handle the current case volume… so we’ll be paying for more officers, but unable to handle more cases.

      Poverty creates desperation, which drives crime. Federal funding cuts, rising homelessness, higher
      insurance costs, plus skyrocketing food prices will directly lead to more poverty in our community.
      Schools, social workers, nonprofits, etc. are also struggling with tight budgets—why should a police force
      that can’t make use of its existing budget be prioritized?

      To prevent crime, we need to invest in programs that keep us fed, housed, and healthy—not more police
      officers on a force that can’t fill already-funded roles, in a system that can’t handle its current case load.

      Hello, I'm writing today about the new proposed "public safety sales tax" being discussed by the council.
      In November, voters approved a policy to increase property tax by 15 cents to cover 13 full time officers,
      gear, and vehicles.
      Previous to that, voters in 2024 rejected a property tax levy by 41 cents for every $1000 of accessed
      value.

      Going around voters to increase sales tax to do this feels very wrong. I understand that House Bill 2015
      allowed the council to increase sales tax, but the voters do not want that and they previously made that
      clear in the 2024 vote. If this sales tax increase was put to a vote in the public, I do not believe it would
      pass. People are struggling on a daily basis to survive and sales tax increases hurt the lower income tax
      bracket far harder than those who are more comfortable. This is not the right time to increase sales tax.

      The Vancouver police department has ample funds but is unable to secure new officers to fill the current
      open roles. This seems to be an internal issue and giving them more money to buy additional military
      grade equipment and yet still have open positions feels silly.

      Ask the police department to fill the open positions they have and then potentially at a later date
      rediscuss if they need additional funding. At this time, they do not.

      Please do not vote in an increase to sales tax for something that police do not need at this time. This is
      not transparent and it is not what the voters want.

Subject
Construction Acceptance - 2025 Pavement Repairs

Key Points

    • The City maintains approximately 1,900 lane miles of streets in its system.
    • Project repaired areas of failed pavement on streets that were identified in the annual
      pavement preservation program.
    • Final construction cost for the project was $1,380,865.48.
    • This project did not have an apprenticeship utilization goal.


Strategic Plan Alignment
Transportation and Mobility – a safe, future-ready and convenient transportation system

Present Situation
This project repaired areas of failed pavement on streets that are being treated in the 2025 pavement
preservation and resurfacing projects. The pavement repairs included planing of roadways, paving of
existing roads, utility adjustments, and temporary striping. Lakeside Industries of Vancouver,
Washington, has satisfactorily completed the subject improvements in accordance with the plans and
specifications.

The original contract amount was $1,287,444.00. The final construction cost was $1,380,865.48, an
increase of approximately 7.3% from the original bid amount. This cost increase can be attributed to
an increase in the flagging quantity, which was necessary to safely perform the work.

The apprenticeship utilization goal for this project was waived pursuant to City policy due to the
following conditions: the project is less than 30 calendar days or working days in duration and will
render apprentice utilization infeasible at the required levels.

Advantage(s)

    1. Completes the City’s contractual and statutory process for accepting the project.
    2. Formal project acceptance allows for closure on third-party bond claims and facilitates release
       of the Contractor’s bond.


Challenge(s)
None

Budget Impact


                                                                                             Page 104 of 578
This project was funded by the Pavement Management Program in the Street Fund.

Prior Council Review
Staff Report 079-25, award of bid for 2025 Pavement Repair Project on April 21, 2025.

Action Requested
On September 14, 2026, accept the 2025 Pavement Repair Project as constructed by Lakeside
Industries of Vancouver, Washington, and authorize release of retainage bond, subject to receipt of
all documentation required by law.

      City streets receive curb-to-curb rehabilitation.

      2025 Resurfacing Project in mid-May, began work in early July 2025, and was physically
      complete in December 2025.
    • The project had a 15% apprenticeship goal. Due to difficulty hiring traffic control and flagging
      apprentices, the contractor submitted and was approved for their Good Faith Effort Request for
      this project.


Strategic Plan Alignment
Transportation and Mobility – a safe, future-ready and convenient transportation system

Present Situation
This project rehabilitated streets in the Rose Village, Vancouver Heights, and Oakbrook
Neighborhoods, as well as along Old Evergreen Highway from SE 164th Avenue to the Eastern City
Limits. The work resurfaced approximately 18 lane miles of asphalt concrete pavement and 15,000
tons of asphalt concrete mix.

Granite Construction Company of Vancouver, Washington has satisfactorily completed the subject
improvements in accordance with the plans and specifications. The original contract amount was
$3,334,355.00. The final construction cost was $3,029,605.97, a decrease of approximately 9.1%
from the original bid amount. This decrease can be attributed to fewer than expected flagging hours
and asphalt quantities.

There was an apprenticeship requirement of 15% for this project. To fulfill the apprenticeship
requirement, the contractor needed a minimum of 382 hours. The contractor was unable to meet this
goal due to difficulty hiring traffic control and flagging apprentices and the large number of trucking
companies involved in this type of work. The contractor recognized the difficulty of meeting the overall
required 15% apprenticeship goal early in the project and began working with the City to document
and submit a Good Faith Effort Request for this project, which was approved by the City.

Strategic Plan Alignment
Safe and Prepared Community – a safe place to live, work, learn and play

Present Situation
The existing utility easement was recorded in 1981 to protect public water and sewer facilities that
extend west into Parcel No. 147389000 from NW Fruit Valley Road. The existing easement extends
significantly beyond the end of the public facilities. The currently vacant west portion of the parcel will
be split off through a boundary line adjustment, combined with the adjoining parcel (Parcel No.
147390000), and developed.

The owner of PIN 147389000, Vancouver Public Schools, has agreed to grant a private building
sewer easement for the new development on PIN 147390000 if the unused portion of the existing
public easement is vacated. This will allow the development to connect to public sewer within PIN
147389000, rather than routing privately-owned sewer facilities within public right-of-way in NW 61st
Street and Fruit Valley Road.

This partial release of the public utility easement will not be recorded until the new private easement
over PIN 147389000 is recorded.

Advantage(s)

       thereby avoiding the need to route private facilities in the public right of way.

Subject
Contract - Seventh Amendment to Professional Services Agreement with First Forty Feet - C-100846

Key Points

    • The City entered into a contract with First Forty Feet (FFF) on March 14, 2022, to lead the
      design of the public infrastructure envisioned in the Heights District Plan.
    • The contract has been amended several times to extend the termination date and to advance
      the design of the first two phases of public infrastructure from preliminary to final design.
    • The contract needs to be amended again to support the construction of the Grand Loop and
      Civic Plaza.


Strategic Plan Alignment
Transportation and Mobility – a safe, future-ready and convenient transportation system

Vibrant and Distinct Neighborhoods – a variety of accessible places and spaces

Present Situation
The City entered into a professional services contract with urban design firm, First Forty Feet, on
March 14, 2022 (Attachment H), to lead the design of the public infrastructure in the Heights District.
Due to the scale and complexity of this project, the contract has been amended several times to
extend the termination date and to advance the design of the first two phases of public infrastructure
from preliminary to final construction ready design. The contract amendments are attached as
exhibits B-H.

Over the course of this professional services contract, the City completed the design of three roadway
projects - Mill Plain Blvd/ MacArthur Blvd intersection; the first phase of the Grand Loop and the
MacArthur Blvd/ Lieser Road intersection. The Mill Plain/MacArthur intersection project is now under
construction and scheduled to be completed in summer 2027. The Grand Loop project is fully funded
and scheduled to start construction in spring 2027. Construction of the Civic Plaza is planned to begin
in 2028 alongside the Grand Loop to maximize construction efficiencies, minimize disruption to the
same area and avoid damage or rework to the Grand Loop that could result from constructing the
plaza at a later date.

To facilitate the construction of the Grand Loop and Civic Plaza, the contract needs to be amended
again. The scope of work under this contract amendment is as follows.

    1. Noise analysis report required by the Washington State Department of Transportation to
       complete the environmental permitting work for the Grand Loop project. This was an
       unforeseen scope of work and required to obligate federal grant funding.
    2. Additional design work to complete the design of the following projects. The location and

                                                                                             Page 125 of 578
       boundaries of these projects are shown in Attachment I - Current Infrastructure Projects
       Delineation Map.
           a. Grand Loop (colored purple)
           b. Mill Plain Blvd/Devine Road intersection (colored orange)
           c. Civic Plaza (colored green)
    3. Bidding and construction support for the Grand Loop (which is required by the engineer of
       record)
    4. Bidding and construction support for the Civic Plaza (which is required by the engineer of
       record)


Advantage(s)
This contract amendment will provide the necessary design, bidding documentation and construction
support to construct the Grand Loop and Civic Plaza, two pivotal pieces of public infrastructure which
support development of the Heights District.

Challenge(s)
None. Anticipated challenges have been mitigated in the scope of work.

Budget Impact
The total cost of this contract amendment is $1,332,161 and will be funded by Public Works and
Parks, Recreation and Cultural Services (PRCS) budgets. There is no budget impact to Public Works
for the transportation and utility related work – the costs will be covered with existing budget. The
Civic Plaza work will be funded using projected revenue from PRCS’s allocation of Business License
Surcharge revenues and existing PRCS budget, subject to the approval of the FY 2027-2028 budget.

Project Description and Background
The adopted Heights District Plan is the culmination of more than two and a half years of public
engagement and participation in a planning process resulting in a community vision for how the
Heights District will develop over the next 20 years.

The Heights District is envisioned as a vibrant neighborhood center that is sustainable, healthy,
equitable, accessible, and safe. The district includes a variety of public open spaces, diverse mixed-
income, mixed-use housing typologies, affordable to a wide range of community members, safe
multi-modal mobility opportunities and access to transit. In addition, neighborhoods around The
Heights District represent the spectrum of the City’s social and economic diversity with both affluent
and economically vulnerable residents. The Heights District Plan is an opportunity for the COV to
partner with the private sector to bring new investment to central Vancouver and ensure that new
development provides benefits and opportunities to a broad range of residents and businesses now
and into the future.

The Heights District Plan is guided by policy and regulatory documents that provide specific
guidance for the Project limits.

II. General Project Organization and Management Provision
Project Management Team
The Heights Grand Loop bidding and construction administration effort will be overseen by a
Project Management Team (PMT) consisting of the City of Vancouver (COV) Heights District Project
Manager, members of the City’s Construction Management Group, other COV staff identified by the
COV Project Manager, and the Consultant Leadership Team (CLT). The CLT will be led by First Forty
Feet (FFF) as prime consultant and will include key support staff and subconsultants, as needed, to
support bidding, construction coordination, design clarification, and construction phase review.

Project Delivery Team
The project will be managed day-to-day through a Project Delivery Team (PDT) consisting of the
COV Heights District Project Manager, the City’s Construction Management Group, and other City
staff identified by the COV Project Manager. First Forty Feet will work directly with this group
throughout bidding and construction to support coordination, track action items, resolve project
questions, and maintain alignment between the design intent and field implementation.

Technical Coordination
During bidding and construction, FFF will coordinate with the City to identify the appropriate City
departments, utility representatives, and agency staff needed to support technical review and issue
resolution. Rather than a formal technical advisory structure focused on planning-phase milestone
review, technical coordination during this phase will focus on construction implementation,
submittal review, bid and RFI responses, field conditions, and interdepartmental coordination as
needed.

Assumptions
First Forty Feet, as lead consultant, will provide overall project management and coordination for
bidding and construction administration services. FFF will work closely with the City’s Construction
Management Group to oversee project tasks, schedules, submittal workflows, design clarifications,
and decision-making during implementation.

The FFF team will conduct regular coordination meetings with the City and project team throughout
active bidding and construction and will also participate in broader project management meetings
as needed to support schedule tracking, issue resolution, and consultant coordination. The City will
lead contractor management and construction oversight, while FFF will support the City by helping
maintain continuity with the approved design intent and by providing timely responses related to
design interpretation and implementation.
