Subtask 1.4: Quality Assurance/Quality Control (Update)
The First Forty Feet Team will provide quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) services for
bidding support and construction administration activities in accordance with the Consultant’s
QA/QC Program. QA/QC efforts during this phase will focus on maintaining consistency with the
approved design intent, supporting accurate interpretation of the construction documents, and
helping the City respond effectively to questions and issues that arise during procurement and
construction.

The First Forty Feet Team’s QA/QC process will ensure that appropriate, right-sized review measures
are in place at key points throughout bidding and construction. This will include review of addenda,
responses to bidder questions, submittals, RFIs, substitution requests, clarification sketches, field
recommendations, and punch list documentation. Dustin Cooley of APEX will serve as QA/QC
manager and will provide senior-level oversight informed by his experience working with the City of
Vancouver on similar public improvement projects.

The QA/QC process will remain active throughout the delivery of the work and will be integrated
into the project schedule and coordination workflow. Senior design and technical staff will be
involved at appropriate milestones to verify that project responses are technically sound,
coordinated across disciplines, and aligned with the intended character and functionality of the
Grand Loop improvements. This approach will help ensure that construction-phase decisions are
made efficiently and that the quality of the built project reflects the goals established in the
approved design documents.

Subtask 5.3.2.7 Noise Analysis and Report (New)
A traffic noise analysis is required for all federally funded projects that meet FHWA requirements.
Because this project will result in new roadways in new locations, it meets the FHWA and WSDOT
requirements for a detailed noise analysis. This project is part of the new Heights District Masterplan
development and therefore, currently there are limited noise sensitive properties at the site. The site
is also bound by major arterial roadways, East Mill Plain Boulevard, and MacArthur Boulevard, which
are currently the dominant traffic noise sources in the area, and are likely to remain the dominant
traffic noise source in the future.

Acoustics Introduction and Regulatory Review
Provide a summary introduction to acoustics, including information on noise in dense residential
developments and general building acoustic insulation options for residences. Summarize WSDOT
regulations along with those from the City of Vancouver, Clark County and the State of Washington
Administrative Code (WAC).
Land Use Review and Noise Monitoring
MMA will conduct a reconnaissance of the project area to identify all land use types and locate
noise-sensitive properties within approximately 300 feet of the project area as described in the
Procedures for Abatement of Highway Traffic Noise and Construction Noise. Physical and terrain
features that affect noise propagation and features that may be altered during construction shall be
identified. Desing drawings and proposed plans for the proposed development will be obtained
from the project design team and used in this analysis.
Noise measurements and traffic counts will be conducted at three (3) sites as needed to calibrate
the traffic noise model and to ensure a complete description of existing noise levels that are
representative of the land uses along the proposed alignments. The three measurements will be
taken during normal daytime hours with normal free flowing traffic on the nearby arterial roadways.
An illustration of area land use and measurement locations on vicinity maps will be produced for
reference.
Noise Level Modeling and Impact Analysis
This task include construction of existing and future noise models using the FHWA Traffic Noise
Model (TNM, version 2.5). The initial step is to model the traffic noise levels at the three noise
monitoring validation sites using the using the existing roadway configurations and the traffic



                                                     9                                       July 20, 2026

                                                                                              Page 138 of 578
The Heights District Project Scope of Work and Fee
City of Vancouver


counts from the noise measurement survey described above. The sound level predictions will be
compared with the measured sound levels to reach a close agreement of ± 2 dB.
         Existing and Future No-Build: Under the existing and Future No-Build alternatives there
         would be no Heights District Masterplan, and therefore none of the development related
         noise sensitive properties would exist. Therefore, based on the site visits, aerial mapping,
         land use inspection noise sensitive properties surrounding the site will be identified and
         included in this phase of the study. Modeling sites will, at the least, include the Vancouver
         Early Childhood Center, parts of the McLoughlin Middle School, the Park Hill Cemetery and
         any other sensitive properties identified during site visits and land use assessment.
         Using the validated model, existing peak hour traffic volumes from project traffic engineers
         will be used with posted speed limits to calculate existing peak hour noise levels. Traffic
         noise level projections will also be performed for the same sites using the future No-Build
         traffic volumes. These predicted noise levels will be used in comparison with the future Build
         noise levels and to aid in the understanding of the potential change in project area noise
         levels.
         Future Build Conditions: Future Build noise levels during peak hour will also be modeled at
         the same selected noise-sensitive sites above with additional sites based on the proposed
         new and improved roadways and planned Heights District Masterplan development. Based
         on the proposed layout of the Heights District Masterplan, a set of representative noise
         modeling sites will be located throughout the new development. Frequently, one modeling
         location will be used to represent several nearby locations expected to have similar or
         slightly lower noise levels than the modeling location. Planned upper floor units in new
         developments at the site will be included in this analysis. The number of modeling sites will
         be sufficient to accurately predict existing and future (year 2040) No-Build and future Build
         traffic noise levels, identify all potential traffic noise impacts, and if necessary, evaluate traffic
         noise abatement measures.
         Traffic volumes for the new interior roadways will be predicted using average daily trips to
         and from the new development with the traffic distributed along project roadways. Future
         traffic volumes for other roadways, including East Mill Plain Boulevard, MacArthur Boulevard,
         and North Devine Road will be provided directly from the traffic engineers.
         The future Build traffic noise levels will be compared to the approach or exceed noise criteria
         using the WSDOT policy. For residences and churches, noise impacts occur if future traffic
         noise levels approach or exceed 66 dBA Leq during peak hours. The substantial increase
         criteria of 10 dB over the existing conditions will not be applicable for this project in new
         residences at the Heights District Masterplan, but could be applicable to other existing
         sensitive land uses in the area.
         Noise Abatement: Per WSDOT and FHWA policy, abatement must be considered for all
         noise impacts to determine if reasonable and feasible abatement is possible. Although the
         current plans do not support the possibility of reasonable and feasible abatement, it still
         must be evaluated as part of the study. At this time, based on the most current design




                                                       10                                            July 20, 2026

                                                                                                      Page 139 of 578
The Heights District Project Scope of Work and Fee
City of Vancouver


         drawings, expected traffic volumes and speeds, no noise abatement is likely to meet WSDOT
         requirements for reasonable and feasible abatement.


Technical Report
A noise technical report will be prepared. The contents will include an introduction to acoustics,
summary of criteria and regulations, land use, predicted noise levels, and new development
mitigation strategies. Tables and figures will be prepared to aid in the understanding of noise levels
throughout the development. Construction noise will be discussed.
The initial report will be submitted in Microsoft (MS) Word format for review and comments. After
addressing any comments, a final report will be produced in PDF electronic format.

Task 10: Bidding & Construction Support Services - Civic Plaza (New)

Civic Plaza construction administration support is assumed to occur over a 9-month construction
period.
Subtask 10.1 - Bidding Support
First Forty Feet and the consultant team will provide bidding support to assist the City during
contractor procurement. Services may include responding to bidder questions related to design
intent; assisting the City with interpretation of plaza, landscape, festival lane, lighting, paving, planting,
site furnishings, and other visible public realm elements; attending one pre-bid meeting; reviewing
proposed substitutions related to visible public realm elements; supporting the preparation of up to
two addenda; and providing bid review support. Bidding support will focus on items that affect the
Civic Plaza’s public realm character, usability, constructability, and long-term performance.

Deliverables:

         •    Written responses to bidder questions.
         •    Addenda language or exhibits for City review and issuance.
         •    Substitution review comments, if needed.


Subtask 10.2: Submittal and Shop Drawing Review
During construction, the consultant team will receive, and review material submittals, shop drawings,
schedules, samples, mock-ups, and other contractor submittals required under the construction
contract to evaluate general conformance with the contract documents and approved Civic Plaza
design intent. The consultant team will review standard submittals and shop drawings and provide
written comments to the City in accordance with the applicable approval requirements within ten (10)
business days from receipt of complete contractor submissions. More complex or multi-discipline
reviews may require additional review time to coordinate with manufacturers, fabricators, suppliers,
or specialty consultants to verify design consistency, constructability, and compatibility with the
intended public realm character of the Civic Plaza.

Submittals may include, but are not limited to:

          •   Manufacturer’s Certificates of Compliance.
          •   Certificates of Material Origin.
          •   Product data and cut sheets.
          •   Qualified Product List documentation.

       • Paving, concrete finish, and hardscape material submittals.
       • Planting, soil, mulch, and landscape material submittals.

Subtask 10.3: Submittals, RFIs, and Design Clarifications
First Forty Feet and the consultant team will provide focused construction administration support
during active construction to assist the City with design interpretation, coordination, and
implementation of the Civic Plaza. Services may include review of selected material submittals,
product data, shop drawings, mock-ups, and samples for key visible plaza elements; responses to RFIs
and contractor clarification requests; preparation of supplemental sketches or written clarifications,
as needed; review of substitutions affecting design intent; and coordination of responses among
landscape, civil, lighting, and other applicable public realm design disciplines. The team may also
assist the City with draft change order exhibits related to design clarifications, if requested.
Construction administration review will focus on elements that shape the Civic Plaza’s public realm
character and long-term performance, including special paving and surface treatments, landscape
materials, planting, soils, irrigation, site furnishings, seating, festival lane paving and transitions, walls,
railings, bollards, signage, lighting interfaces, and other visible site elements affecting the public
realm.

Subtask 10.4: Construction Phase Coordination
FFF will work closely with the City’s Construction Management Group during active construction to
support coordination, issue resolution, and continuity between the approved Civic Plaza design and
field implementation. Coordination during this phase will focus on construction sequencing, plaza
access, festival lane interface conditions, public realm improvements, landscape installation, lighting
coordination, and the relationship between Civic Plaza work and adjacent roadway or developer
construction activities. FFF will participate in construction-related coordination discussions as needed
to help identify design-related issues early, support timely decisions, and minimize conflicts between
plaza construction, public access, adjacent development activity, and related infrastructure work.

Consultant responsibilities will include attending the pre-construction meeting with the City,
Contractor, and consultant team; participating in periodic construction coordination meetings with
the City’s Construction Management Group during active construction; coordinating with the City and
consultant team regarding action items, schedule impacts, submittal status, field decisions, and
design-related construction issues; and supporting timely communication regarding construction
phasing, access constraints, adjacent developer coordination, and overlap with road contractor
activities that may affect implementation of the Civic Plaza.

Subtask 10.5: Site Observation and Construction Administration Support
First Forty Feet and the consultant team will provide limited site observation during construction to
review general conformance with the approved design intent and support the City during
implementation of the Civic Plaza. These services are intended to assist with design continuity and
field coordination and do not replace City inspection, contractor quality control, required special
inspections, or the contractor’s responsibility for means, methods, sequencing, and safety. Site
observation may include review of plaza layout and pedestrian circulation, festival lane interfaces,
paving transitions, accessibility conditions, landscape areas, trees, planting, irrigation, site furnishings,
seating, walls, railings, bollards, lighting, power, utility interface items, and overall public realm quality.


Deliverables:
       • Site observation notes.
       • Design-related field comments.
       • Follow-up action items, if needed.


Subtask 10.6: Punch List and Closeout Support
At substantial completion, First Forty Feet and the consultant team will assist the City with punch list
and closeout review for the designed Civic Plaza elements. Services may include participation in one
substantial completion walk-through; preparation of design-related punch list comments; review of
completed punch list items; participation in one final back-check walk-through; review of selected
closeout documents related to landscape, irrigation, site furnishings, lighting, and other designed
public realm elements; and preparation of final design-related closeout comments for the City. This
work is intended to support final review of the Civic Plaza’s public realm quality, usability, landscape
performance, and overall completion prior to final acceptance.

           Introduction
           The First Forty Feet (FFF) Consultant Team have been selected by the City of Vancouver (COV or
           City) to prepare construction and permitting documents for the Heights District public

           Consultant Leadership Team (CLT), inclusive of key personnel from First Forty Feet, APEX, and

           Subtask 5.3.2.5 Cultural Resources (AINW) (Update)
           Archaeological Investigations Northwest, Inc. (AINW) has completed a report titled Cultural
           Resources Survey for the Heights District Infrastructure Phase I Project, Vancouver, Clark County,
           Washington, also known as the Loop Roads project. On April 28, 2025, the Washington State
           Department of Archaeology and Historic Preservation (DAHP) concurred with the findings in the
           report, including AINW’s recommendation that an adverse effect on historic properties would
           occur under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.

           To complete the Section 106 consultation process, resolution of adverse effects must be agreed
           upon in a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between FHWA and DAHP, with WSDOT and the City
           signing as concurring parties. The completed MOA will be included in the individual Section 4(f)
           evaluation for Vanco Driving Range (see Subtask 5.3.2.6) and is needed to close out NEPA review.

           AINW will develop ideas for resolving adverse effects (i.e., mitigation measures) and will meet
           with City and consultant staff to assist with narrowing alternatives to a list of preferred actions.
           AINW staff will also participate in meetings with WSDOT and DAHP staff to discuss and negotiate
           the City’s preferred mitigation measures.

           Assumptions:
                x   WSDOT will draft the MOA and circulate it for review and signatures.
                x   Participation in up to four meetings is anticipated to assist the City with negotiating the
                    MOA and mitigation measures with WSDOT, FHWA, and DAHP.

           Deliverables:
                x   Draft and final list of proposed mitigation measures for delivery to WSDOT.

           Subtask 5.3.2.6 Section 4(f) Evaluation (APEX, FFF, and AINW) (New)
           Understanding and Background
           Section 4(f) of the Department of Transportation Act of 1966 mandates special considerations for
           certain resources when approving transportation projects that receive federal funding. Section
           4(f) applies when transportation projects that receive federal funding "use" properties protected
           by the U.S. Department of Transportation Act. This includes publicly owned parks, recreation
           areas, wildlife and waterfowl refuges, and historic sites. The "use" of a Section 4(f) property must
           be evaluated to ensure that the project considers ways to minimize harm to the property and to
           determine if any feasible and prudent alternative exists.

             Amendment No. 6


                                                                                                         Page 169 of 578

 $#% !  
                                     
                                           
                                                  
                                                         




           Section 4(f) is a federal requirement that must be considered in any NEPA document involving a
           US Department of Transportation (USDOT) agency (Federal Highway Administration [FHWA],
           Federal Transit Administration, Federal Rail Administration, and Federal Aviation Administration),
           and it prohibits the incorporation of land from a Section 4(f) resource into a transportation
           facility unless there is no feasible and prudent alternative to the use of that land.

           The Heights District Phase I Infrastructure Project aka Loop Roads will receive federal funds from
           the FHWA distributed through the Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) Local
           Programs.

           In general, a Section 4(f) use occurs when:

                x     Section 4(f) land is permanently incorporated into a transportation facility (permanent
                      use);
                x     There is a temporary occupancy of Section 4(f) land that is adverse in terms of the Section
                      4(f) preservation purposes (temporary occupancy); or
                x     Section 4(f) land is not incorporated into the transportation project, but the project’s
                      proximity impacts are so severe that the protected activities, features, or attributes that
                      qualify a resource for protection under Section 4(f) are substantially impaired
                      (constructive use).

           The Loop Roads project will permanently incorporate the Vanco Driving Range into a
           transportation facility. The Vanco Driving Range was recommended eligible under Criteria A and
           C for listing on the National Register Historic Places (NHRP) by Archaeological Investigations
           Northwest, Inc. (AINW) in their report titled Cultural Resources Survey for the Heights District
           Infrastructure Phase I Project, Vancouver, Clark County, Washington. On April 28, 2025, the
           Washington State Department of Archaeology and Historic Preservation (DAHP) concurred that
           the Vanco Driving Range (Property ID: 735618) was eligible for listing on the NRHP. The removal
           of Vanco is a use of a historic site and is required to be evaluated under Section 4(f).

           Scope of Work
           The Section 4(f) Evaluation report will be completed to evaluate the resources protected by
           Section 4(f) and the Vanco Driving Range will be the resource evaluated. The report will describe
           Section 4(f) resources in the project vicinity, use of those resources by the Preferred Alternative
           and other build alternatives, measures to minimize harm, an analysis of least overall harm, and
           provide a description of coordination efforts to protect Section 4(f) resources. APEX will prepare
           the 4(f) Evaluation with support from First Forty Feet and AINW. A breakdown of the Section 4(f)
           tasks including roles and responsibilities of the project team is below:

            Project Description and Background
            The adopted Heights District Plan is the culmination of more than two and a half years of public engagement and participation in a
            planning process resulting in a community vision for how the Heights District will develop over the next 20 years.

            The Heights District is envisioned as a vibrant neighborhood center that is sustainable, healthy, equitable, accessible, and safe. The
            district includes a variety of public open spaces, diverse mixed-income, mixed-use housing typologies, affordable to a wide range of
            community members, safe multi-modal mobility opportunities and access to transit. In addition, neighborhoods around The Heights
            District represent the spectrum of the City’s social and economic diversity with both affluent and economically vulnerable residents.
            The Heights District Plan is an opportunity for the COV to partner with the private sector to bring new investment to central
            Vancouver and ensure that new development provides benefits and opportunities to a broad range of residents and businesses now
            and into the future.

            The Heights District Plan is guided by policy and regulatory documents that provide specific guidance for the Project limits.

            Subtask 4.6: Geotechnical Engineering
            The Civic Plaza stage canopy and structure will likely require selective geotechnical investigations. The task will include inspection of
            geotechnical investigations to document subsurface conditions in locations of the civic plaza building and/or the stage canopy
            structure.

            Subtask 4.6.1: Geotechnical Site Evaluations
            Current project plans include infrastructure design to support the future buildout of multiple City blocks. Development will include
            improvements within the Civic Plaza in support of structures and stormwater within the site. Future buildout will require disposal of
            stormwater collected on City streets and will likely be accomplished using onsite infiltration. PBS’ current plans are to complete
            borings within the proposed Civic Place area to develop foundation recommendations for structures and complete on-site infiltration
            testing. PBS will provide input regarding appropriate standard pavement sections based on soil type and consistency/relative density.

            Subtask 4.6.2: Geologic Map Review (No Change)

            Subtask 4.6.3: Subsurface Exploration (Updated)
            Subsurface conditions will be explored by completing four borings, including two borings to depths of up to 30 feet below the
            existing ground surface (bgs) for the new structure and two borings to depths of up to 10 feet bgs for the courtyard, using a truck-
            mounted drill rig. Borings will be advanced to the indicated depths or practical refusal of the drilling equipment, whichever occurs
            first. In situ, standard penetration tests will be performed at 2.5- to 5-foot intervals. The borings will be logged, observed
            groundwater levels noted, and representative soil samples collected by a member of the PBS geotechnical engineering staff. Cuttings
            will be drummed and disposed of offsite.

            Subtask 4.6.4: Piezometer Installation (No Change)




                                                                                 9                                                         August 15, 2024

                                                                                                                                                    Page 184 of 578
                           




                                                                                                                                                                       Docusign Envelope ID: 03C23412-BAFB-42AB-B207-CFE5D319376F
            The Heights District Project Scope of Work and Fee
            City of Vancouver


            Subtask 4.6.5: Field Infiltration Testing
            Up to two infiltration tests will be completed, one each in the 10-foot borings, at depths between 4 to 6 feet bgs. A soil sample will be
            collected at each boring immediately below the infiltration test depth for laboratory testing. Explorations will be extended up to 5
            feet below the infiltration test depth.

            Subtask 4.6.6: Soils Testing
            Samples will be returned to our laboratory and classified by the Unified Soil Classification System (ASTM D2487) and/or the Visual-
            Manual Procedure (ASTM D2488). Laboratory tests may include natural moisture contents, Atterberg limits, and grain-size analyses, as
            appropriate.

            Subtask 4.6.7: Geotechnical Engineering Analyses
            The data collected during the subsurface exploration, literature research, and testing will be analyzed to develop geotechnical
            recommendations for design and construction.

            Assumptions:
                x    Soil samples collected during the explorations will be stored for a minimum of 60 days after completion of subsurface
                     exploration. Additional storage time may be requested for a monthly fee.

            Task 5: Permitting (Update)
            The project area is known not to contain critical areas or other regulated sensitive areas. The completion of critical area assessments
            or permitting outside of that typically required for civil infrastructure projects will not be necessary. As the initial master plans for the
            project were reviewed under the SEPA EIS process, the project will not require further review under SEPA unless there has been a
            significant change in the plans compared to what was initially reviewed.

            When federal monies are made available the project will be required to comply with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).
            Based on the proposed project timeline, the NEPA review process will be initiated during further refinement beyond 30% without
            impacting delivery and construction timeframes. At this time only the Mill Plain & MacArthur project will be receiving federal
            funding with the following NEPA scope supporting those documents and coordination with WSDOT Local Programs to obtain
            funding approval milestones. The City will be responsible for contracting with a Right-of-Way subcontractor to support required
            documentation in conjunction with obtaining funding approvals for acquisition.

            Amendment 3 (Draft)

            Introduction
             The First Forty Feet (FFF) Consultant Team have been selected by the City of Vancouver (COV or City) to
            prepare construction and permitting documents for the Heights District public infrastructure, henceforth
            referenced as the Heights District Project and described further throughout the scope of work as “Project”.
            The scope of work will include Mill Plain Blvd & MacArthur Blvd intersection (green), northern section of the
            Grand Loop with associated internal street (orange), eastern section of the Grand Loop with associated
            internal street (red), and Leiser roundabout (blue). The scope of work will include design development, 100%
            construction documentation, urban design specifications, continued key stakeholder and community
            engagement, arts integration, land use planning, traffic and design engineering, SEPA and environmental
            analysis.

            Professional services for the Project will include update of the masterplan (Tower Mall Redevelopment Area),
            evaluation of site development configuration options, traffic engineering, evaluation of roundabouts and
            traffic signals, lighting designs, park design, landscape designs, structural designs, environmental process and
            permits, and utilities coordination and design. Coordination of services and deliverables will integrate with and
            support the Equitable Development Plan project’s recommended strategies and tools for culturally relevant
            and inclusive programming within the District and funding strategies to support one-time infrastructure and
            ongoing programmatic investments required to ensure equitable development of the Heights over the long-
            term. Additionally, project coordination and required federal documentation will be performed.

            The Project team includes:
                 •     First Forty Feet – Overall Project Management, Urban Design, Placemaking and Streetscape
                      Specifications/Guidelines, Grand Loop Design, and Communications and Engagement support.
                 •    PBS Engineering and Environmental Inc. – Civil Design Documentation, Traffic Engineering,
                      Intersection Design, Traffic Signal Design, Lighting Design, Stormwater Design & Specifications, Utility
                      Design, Permitting, and Communications support, Landscape Architecture, Planting Design, and
                      Irrigation.
                 •    DCW – Cost Management and Cost Estimating


            Project Description and Background
            The adopted Heights District Plan is the culmination of more than two and a half years of public engagement
            and participation in a planning process resulting in a community vision for how the Heights District will
            develop over the next 20 years.

            The Heights District is envisioned as a vibrant neighborhood center that is sustainable, healthy, equitable,
            accessible, and safe. The district includes a variety of public open spaces, diverse mixed-income, mixed-use
            housing typologies, affordable to a wide range of community members, safe multi-modal mobility
            opportunities and access to transit. In addition, neighborhoods around The Heights District represent the

            spectrum of the City’s social and economic diversity with both affluent and economically vulnerable residents.
            The Heights District Plan is an opportunity for the COV to partner with the private sector to bring new
            investment to central Vancouver and ensure that new development provides benefits and opportunities to a
            broad range of residents and businesses now and into the future.

            The Heights District Plan is guided by policy and regulatory documents that provide specific guidance for the
            Project limits.


            Project Scope of Work
            The First Forty Feet Team will work with the City of Vancouver to provide public outreach and prepare the final
            master plan, construction drawings, specifications, cost estimates, permit documents and provide bidding and
            construction support.

            The Project will complete master planning, construction, and permitting documents, for the development of
            public infrastructure including roadways, utilities, public spaces, wayfinding, and transit amenities within the
            63-acre TMRA.

            The following amended scope of work tasks describes how the Consultant Team will collaborate with the COV
            project manager, city staff, key stakeholders, community members, and regulatory agencies to progress
            beyond the original 30% design phase select prioritized projects to the final design as individual bundled
            plans, specs, and estimates (PS&E) for future advertisement.
                 1.   Mill Plain Blvd and MacArthur Blvd Intersection
                 1.   MacArthur Blvd and Lieser Road Intersection
                 2.   North TMRA Loop Road
                 3.   East TMRA Loop Road

            II. General Project Organization and Management Provision
            Project Management Team
            The Heights Project will have oversight by a Project Management Team (PMT) comprised of the COV Heights
            District Project Manager, COV staff as identified by the COV Project Manager, and the Consultant Leadership
            Team (CLT), inclusive of key personnel from First Forty Feet, PBS, and DCW Cost Estimating. The CLT is led by
            the prime consultant, First Forty Feet (FFF).

            Project Delivery Teams
            The Heights Project will be organized and managed by a Project Delivery Teams (PDT) comprised of the COV
            Heights District Project Manager, and COV staff as identified by the COV Project Manager

            Technical Advisory Committee
            The FFF team will continue to work with the established Technical Advisory Committee, . The focus of the TAC
            will be to provide review and feedback of analyses and reports at key milestones. where feasible and when
            requested by City staff, to provide data and other resources to supplement the work included in the Project
            scope.

            Subtask 1.4: Quality Assurance/Quality Control (Updated)
            The First Forty Feet Team will provide QA/QC for conceptual design, technical analyses, and construction
            documentation, specifications and permitting work in accordance with the Consultant’s QA/QC Program.
            The First Forty Team’s QA/QC will ensure appropriate, right-sized quality assurance and control measures are
            in place and executed at key points during planning and design efforts. Greg Jellison, of PBS will be the
            QA/QC manager who has worked extensively with the City of Vancouver on similar projects. The QA/QC
            process will be active throughout the life of the delivery process, providing a balance between the Design
            Confirmation (Tasks 2-4) and Design Implementation (Tasks 5-8) phases with technical reviewers involved to
            ensure that technical elements are accounted for during the Design Confirmation phase and that overarching
            themes of the masterplan are not lost during Design Implementation.

            The QA/QC plan will be integrated throughout all processes and woven into our critical path delivery
            schedule; for example, how the use of public spaces and multi-modal facilities throughout the project area will
            be vetted early in the Design Confirmation process will require that the design team support concepts and
            cost estimating processes with additional permitting requirements being accounted for. The First Forty Team
            will have the proper experts involved throughout the project life at varying capacity providing senior level
            design and construction personnel to review deliverables and provide technical support.

            Subtask 1.5: Project Management Team (PMT) Kick-off

            Task 2: Communications Plan (Updated)
            The First Forty Feet Team understands the COV will lead community engagement and communications on this
            project, serving as the face and the main contact for stakeholders and the community at large. The Consultant
            Team will coordinate, with the COV, identification of the necessary stakeholders, methods of outreach,
            engagement, and summary reporting, including a meeting schedule, and facilities or online applications
            necessary and available to support a range of in-person (if desired) and virtual engagement.
            The COV will manage delivery of project updates and information through the targeted use of established
            communications channels, such as the Heights District Plan email list, the City of Vancouver website and social
            media, Be Heard Vancouver engagement platform, Office of Neighborhoods and Vancouver Connects
            newsletters, and My Vancouver app.

            The First Forty Feet Team will prepare necessary planning, design, logistics, content and materials to support
            the COV in communications and outreach efforts.

            PBS, with FFF support, will prepare a Project Communications Plan in coordination with the COV
            Communications team to guide both how the project is communicated and how input is used and shared.
            with the purpose of:
                 •   Outlining the goals for public engagement.
                 •   Specifying the project design and programming elements stakeholder input will inform.
                 •   Detailing methods, techniques, timelines and staffing assignments.

            Subtask 4.6.1: Geotechnical Site Evaluations (No Change)

            Subtask 4.6.3: Subsurface Exploration (Updated)
            Subsurface conditions will be explored at proposed signal poles located at E. Mill Plain Boulevard/MacArthur
            Boulevard and E. Mill Plain Boulevard/N. Devine Road and at two stormwater facility locations along N.
            Andresen Road by completing four (4) additional borings using a truck-mounted drill rig. Borings will be
            advanced to depths of up to 30 feet bgs or practical refusal of the drilling equipment, whichever occurs first.
            In situ, standard penetration tests will be performed at 2.5- to 5-foot intervals. The borings will be logged,
            observed groundwater levels noted, and representative soil samples collected by a member of the PBS
            geotechnical engineering staff. Cuttings will be drummed and disposed of offsite.

            Subtask 4.6.4: Piezometer Installation (No Change)

            Subtask 4.6.5: Field Infiltration Testing (Updated)
            Two (2) cased-hole, falling-head infiltration tests will be completed, one in each boring completed along N
            Andresen Road, at depths of 10 or 20 feet bgs in general accordance with City of Vancouver test procedures.
            A soil sample will be collected immediately below the infiltration test depth for laboratory testing. Borings will
            be extended up to 10 feet below the infiltration test depth.

            Subtask 4.6.6: Soils Testing (Updated)
            Samples will be returned to our laboratory and classified by the Unified Soil Classification System (ASTM
            D2487) and/or the Visual-Manual Procedure (ASTM D2488). Laboratory tests may include natural moisture
            contents, Atterberg limits, and grain-size analyses, as appropriate.

            Subtask 4.6.7: Geotechnical Engineering Analyses (Updated)
            The data collected during the subsurface exploration, literature research, and testing will be analyzed to
            develop geotechnical recommendations for design and construction. The geotechnical engineering report for

            Subtask 4.7: Traffic Engineering (Updated)
            A traffic impact analysis (TIA) memorandum, dated August 30, 2019 by HDR, was prepared for The Heights
            District redevelopment plan. It addresses redevelopment within Zones 1, 2 and 3 in the vicinity of the Tower
            Mall area, which are planned to include 1,340 residential units and 204,000 square feet of commercial space as
            replacement for the existing under-utilized 258,000 square feet of commercial space. The TIA assumed no new
            commercial trips. Between the bus rapid transit (BRT) system currently being built on Mill Plain Boulevard and
            the planned multi-modal transportation improvements within the district, the TIA assumes a 6% reduction in
            trips. The original TIA assumed all new trips to be related to the proposed residential land use. During the AM
            peak hour 400 net new trips are estimated, with 100 entering and 300 exiting. During the PM peak hour 600
            net new trips are estimated, with 370 entering and 230 exiting.

            At the November 30, 2021, meeting, the City expanded the scope of work to include updating the TIA to
            address the replacement of the commercial land uses to the many years of vacant space at the Town Mall.
            The TIA assumed roundabouts will be installed at the MacArthur Boulevard/Andresen Road and MacArthur
            Boulevard/Devine Road intersections.

            To maintain an acceptable level of service at studied intersections, a trip accounting system is proposed to
            verify trips generated by the proposed land uses do not exceed the new trips analyzed in the TIA.

            Task 5: Permitting
            The project area is known not to contain critical areas or other regulated sensitive areas. The completion of
            critical area assessments or permitting outside of that typically required for civil infrastructure projects will not
            be necessary. As the initial master plans for the project were reviewed under the SEPA EIS process, the project
            will not require further review under SEPA unless there has been a significant change in the plans compared to
            what was initially reviewed.

            When federal monies are made available then the project will be required to comply with the National
            Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). Based on the proposed project timeline, the NEPA review process can be
            initiated during further refinement beyond 30% without impacting delivery and construction timeframes.

            Subtask 5.1: Preliminary Permitting Assessment (No Change)

            Subtask 5.2: Permitting Preparation (New)
            PBS will complete the State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) checklist for the project. The SEPA will contain
            information about impacts to natural resources and will include discussions related to the following: air, water,
            plants, wildlife, energy, environmental health, housing, aesthetics, light and glare, historical and cultural
            preservation, transportation, and utilities. The SEPA checklist will be completed with sufficient detail to enable
            city staff to determine if the project has the potential to result in significant environmental impacts.

            Assumptions:
               • No critical areas are present with project area
               • Agency review fees are not included in the PBS compensation amount
               • City will complete one round of comments on Draft SEPA
               • Permitting only required for MacArthur Blvd & Lieser Road Intersection project in support of task 7.2

            Deliverables:
                • Draft and Final SEPA Checklist and attendant graphics

            each utility’s relocation plans with the other utilities in order to maximize compatibility of relocation designs
            and utility and roadway construction sequencing. Meeting agendas and summaries will be prepared and
            transmitted to utility representatives, City, and Consultant team members.

            Utility Coordination
            Contact utilities within the project limits and obtain existing system mapping. Review mapping for
            consistency with project base map.

            Conduct a utility reconnaissance of the project corridor to determine visual evidence of underground and
            above ground utility facilities and confirm utility provided facility maps and project base map
            completeness.

            Identify and discuss with each utility special requirements associated with their facility relocation or
            modification.

            Utility Meetings (Revised)
            Up to three group utility meetings will be organized and facilitated to provide updated project information.
            Such meetings will address known facilities, potential for impact, timing requirements for potential
            relocations, and initial information of reimbursable requirements. Meetings will also allow the exchange of
            each utility’s relocation plans with the other utilities in order to maximize compatibility of relocation designs
            and utility and roadway construction sequencing. Meeting agendas and summaries will be prepared and
            transmitted to utility representatives, City, and Consultant team members.

            Conflict Identification, Analysis and Recommended Resolution (Revised)
            PBS will identify and analyze utility conflicts and compile and distribute utility conflict lists involving
            aboveground, surface, and underground conflicts, and make conflict resolution recommendations to utilities.

            The Consultant will produce utility conflict plan sheets based on 60% design plans and accompanying utility
            conflict spreadsheets indicating conflict item number, type of utility, conflict status, average cover during and
            after construction, whether utility is in or out of public right-of-way, and comments. This subtask assumes four
            (4) different utility operators.
            Finalize conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 90% design plans
            Revise conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 100% design plans

            Conflict Notification and Utility Relocations (Revised)
            Notify the impacted utilities and coordinate the efforts of the utility agencies in developing and executing a
            plan for relocating utilities to resolve conflicts with the project design. As part of that effort:

            Prepare and deliver to each involved utility owner a conflict notice with attached conflict list and map. Assume
            up to four (4) different utility operators. Notice shall require a utility response in the form of a proposed
            facility adjustment plan and schedule to complete the utility work. Allow each utility a 30-day period to
            respond with a proposal from date of the notice.

            Review utilities’ proposed relocation plans to verify that identified conflict items are addressed and that the
            plans accommodate and conform to the construction requirements for the project. Provide written approval
            of each utility’s relocation plan. Up to six (6) total reviews will be performed for the utilities’ relocation plans
            (average 1.5 per utility).

            Utility Coordination & Design
            Contact utilities within the project limits and obtain existing system mapping. Review mapping for
            consistency with project base map.

            Conduct a utility reconnaissance of the project corridor to determine visual evidence of underground and
            above ground utility facilities and confirm utility provided facility maps and project base map
            completeness.

            Identify and discuss with each utility special requirements associated with their facility relocation or
            modification.

            Utility Meetings (Revised)
            Up to three group utility meetings will be organized and facilitated to provide updated project information.
            Such meetings will address known facilities, potential for impact, timing requirements for potential
            relocations, and requirements for service to future development within the TMRA . Meetings will also allow
            the exchange of each utility’s relocation plans with the other utilities in order to maximize compatibility of
            relocation designs and utility and roadway construction sequencing. Meeting agendas and summaries will be
            prepared and transmitted to utility representatives, City, and Consultant team members.

            Conflict Identification, Analysis and Recommended Resolution (Revised)
            PBS will identify and analyze utility conflicts and compile and distribute utility conflict lists involving
            aboveground, surface, and underground conflicts, and make conflict resolution recommendations to utilities.

            The Consultant will produce utility conflict plan sheets based on preliminary (60%) design plans and
            accompanying utility conflict spreadsheets indicating conflict item number, type of utility, conflict status,
            average cover during and after construction, whether utility is in or out of public right-of-way, and comments.
            This subtask assumes four (4) different franchise utility operators.
            Finalize conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 90% design plans
            Revise conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 100% design plans

            Conflict Notification and Utility Relocations (Revised)
            Notify the impacted utilities and coordinate the efforts of the utility agencies in developing and executing a
            plan for relocating utilities to resolve conflicts with the project design. As part of that effort:
            Prepare and deliver to each involved utility owner a conflict notice with attached conflict list and map. Assume
            up to four (4) different utility operators. Notice shall require a utility response in the form of a proposed
            facility adjustment plan and schedule to complete the utility work. Allow each utility a 30-day period to
            respond with a proposal from date of the notice.

            permit application and Notice of Intent (NOI). The NOI will be submitted to the local newspaper. Consultant
            will prepare the Transfer of Coverage and Notice of Termination forms for City and Contractor signature and
            submittal, which will constitute transfer of coverage to the Contractor.
            In addition, Consultant will prepare the SWPPP to be kept at the site during construction.

            Deliverables:
                • Permit Application
                • Notice of Intent (NOI)
                • SWPPP
                • Transfer of Coverage Form
                • Notice of Termination Form

            Utility Coordination & Design
            Contact utilities within the project limits and obtain existing system mapping. Review mapping for
            consistency with project base map.

            Conduct a utility reconnaissance of the project corridor to determine visual evidence of underground and
            above ground utility facilities and confirm utility provided facility maps and project base map
            completeness.

            Identify and discuss with each utility special requirements associated with their facility relocation or
            modification.

            Utility Meetings (Revised)
            Up to three group utility meetings will be organized and facilitated to provide updated project information.
            Such meetings will address known facilities, potential for impact, timing requirements for potential
            relocations, and initial information of reimbursable requirements. Meetings will also allow the exchange of
            each utility’s relocation plans with the other utilities in order to maximize compatibility of relocation designs
            and utility and roadway construction sequencing. Meeting agendas and summaries will be prepared and
            transmitted to utility representatives, City, and Consultant team members.

            Conflict Identification, Analysis and Recommended Resolution (Revised)
            PBS will identify and analyze utility conflicts and compile and distribute utility conflict lists involving
            aboveground, surface, and underground conflicts, and make conflict resolution recommendations to utilities.

            The Consultant will produce utility conflict plan sheets based on preliminary (60%) design plans and
            accompanying utility conflict spreadsheets indicating conflict item number, type of utility, conflict status,
            average cover during and after construction, whether utility is in or out of public right-of-way, and comments.
            This subtask assumes four (4) different utility operators.
            Finalize conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 90% design plans
            Revise conflict analysis and conflict spreadsheets based on 100% design plans

            Conflict Notification and Utility Relocations (Revised)
            Notify the impacted utilities and coordinate the efforts of the utility agencies in developing and executing a
            plan for relocating utilities to resolve conflicts with the project design. As part of that effort:
            Prepare and deliver to each involved utility owner a conflict notice with attached conflict list and map. Assume
            up to six (6) different utility operators. Notice shall require a utility response in the form of a proposed facility
            adjustment plan and schedule to complete the utility work. Allow each utility a 30-day period to respond with
            a proposal from date of the notice.
            Review utilities’ proposed relocation plans to verify that identified conflict items are addressed and that the
            plans accommodate and conform to the construction requirements for the project. Provide written approval
            of each utility’s relocation plan. Up to six (6) total reviews will be performed for the utilities’ relocation plans
            (average 1.5 per utility).

            Assumptions:
               • City will provide utility plans, GIS, and other supporting documents for City utilities within the project
                  corridor.
                 •   PBS will coordinate with upto four franchse utility providers as part of this task (power, phone, cable,
                     gas.

                                                             SCHEDULE 1
                                             DCW COST MANAGEMENT, LLC’s Basic Services
            Project Description:
            We understand that the project comprises cost planning for The Heights District Tower Mall
            Redevelopment Area Public Infrastructure located in Vancouver, WA. The cost study scope of work
            includes costing the 60%, 95%, and 100% design drawings.
            The intended design package consists of linear park elements for the Grand Loop North and East. The
            three-quarter mile Grand Loop involves distinct segments and is designed through the concept of ‘play’
            as an inclusive activity where multiple generations benefit.
            It is complemented by the MacArthur ‘greenbelt’, the Neighborhood Park, and Civic Park (plaza and
            festival street). These areas offer an opportunity for engagement to inform programming and design with
            insight and feedback on how these spaces will be used and what elements are valued. The Parks and
            Recreation Commission, school, neighborhood associations, neighborhood residents, property owners
            and businesses would be oriented to this topic.


            Detailed Scope of Work:
            Task 1 60% Design
                 •    Prepare an opinion of probable construction costs during this stage including all elements as
                      necessary for a complete cost estimate. The cost estimate will be prepared in Uniformat II
                      component format.
                 •    This stage includes a maximum of three alternates.
                 •    Prepare a single revision to the opinion of probable construction cost after review and
                      commentary by the team. Further revision requests are not included and may require additional
                      fee.
                 •    Up to three team and client meetings are included during this phase.


            Task 2 95% Design
                 •    Prepare an opinion of probable construction costs during this stage including all elements as
                      necessary for a complete cost estimate. The cost estimate will be prepared in Uniformat II
                      component format.
                 •    This stage includes a maximum of two alternates.
                 •    Prepare a single revision to the opinion of probable construction cost after review and
                      commentary by the team. Further revision requests are not included and may require additional
                      fee.
                 •    Up to three team and client meetings are included during this phase.


            Task 3 100% Design
                 •    Prepare an opinion of probable construction costs during this stage including all elements as
                      necessary for a complete cost estimate. The cost estimate will be prepared in Uniformat II
                      component format.
                 •    Prepare a single revision to the opinion of probable construction cost after review and
                      commentary by the team. Further revision requests are not included and may require additional
                      fee.
                 •    Up to three team and client meetings are included during this phase.

            Introduction
            The First Forty Feet (FFF) Consultant Team have been selected by the City of Vancouver (COV or City) to
            prepare construction and permitting documents for the Heights District public infrastructure, henceforth
            referenced as the Heights District Project and described further throughout the scope of work as “Project”.
            The scope of work will include design confirmation of planning elements, placemaking strategies, public open
            space design, key stakeholder engagement, land use planning, traffic and design engineering, environmental
            analysis, capital investment strategies and other related professional services as identified in the Request for
            Qualifications (RFQ) #31-21 for the Heights District Tower Mall Redevelopment Area Public Infrastructure
            Master Plan and Construction Documents.

            Concurrent with the Project, COV is managing implementation of an Equitable Development Plan for the
            Heights District. The Equitable Development Plan seeks to prioritize community-identified improvements and
            needs while maximizing community benefits and minimizing displacement risk resulting from these
            investments. For this reason, the City of Vancouver seeks to pair its investments with proactive strategies to
            prevent residential and commercial displacement and ensure that benefits accrue to local residents and
            businesses.

            Professional services for the Project will include evaluation of site development configuration options, traffic
            engineering, evaluation of roundabouts and traffic signals, lighting designs, park design, landscape designs,
            structural designs, environmental process and permits, and utilities coordination and design. Coordination of
            services and deliverables will integrate with and support the Equitable Development Plan project’s
            recommended strategies and tools for culturally relevant and inclusive programming within the District and
            funding strategies to support one-time infrastructure and ongoing programmatic investments required to
            ensure equitable development of the Heights over the long-term. Additionally, project coordination and
            required federal documentation will be performed.

            The Project team includes:
                 •    First Forty Feet – Overall Project Management, Master Planning, Urban Design, Strategic Planning,
                      Placemaking Strategies, Complete Street Design, and Communications support.
                 •    PBS Engineering and Environmental Inc. – Civil Design, Permitting, Grant Funding Opportunities, and
                      Communications Plan.
                 •    Walker Macy – Landscape Architecture, Public Open Space Design, Park Design, and Lighting Design.
                 •    Archaeological Investigations Northwest (AINW) – Cultural Resources Analysis
                 •    DCW – Cost Management and Cost Estimating
                 •    Leland Consulting Group – Capital Investment Strategy and Funding Opportunities.

            The Project is locally funded for design and has potential to receive federal funding for the public
            infrastructure construction phases.

            The Heights District Project Scope of Work and Fee
            City of Vancouver


            The COV has completed an Environmental Impact Statement (Final EIS) for the Heights District Plan. The
            Heights District Plan was initiated by the COV to identify a community-based vision for the area, and to
            catalyze revitalization and private investment in central Vancouver. The Heights District is approximately 205
            acres and includes the 63-acre Tower Mall Redevelopment Area, which includes the 12-acre site of the former
            Tower Mall that was acquired by the COV in 2017.

            The Tower Mall Redevelopment Area (TMRA) is the focus of most of the redevelopment proposed in the Plan.
            For the Tower Mall Redevelopment Area, three concept plans were prepared based on input received during
            an extensive neighborhood and stakeholder engagement process. The initial concepts consisted of The
            Promenade, The Grand Loop, and The Grand Park. Based on community feedback, the concept plans were
            refined and a preferred concept for The Grand Loop was developed, which incorporated elements from all
            three concepts. The Grand Loop concept forms the basis of the Heights District Plan and is part of the Project
            Alternative evaluated in the EIS.


            Project Description and Background
            The adopted Heights District Plan is the culmination of more than two and a half years of public engagement
            and participation in a planning process resulting in a community vision for how the Heights District will
            develop over the next 20 years.

            The Heights District is envisioned as a vibrant neighborhood center that is sustainable, healthy, equitable,
            accessible, and safe. The district includes a variety of public open spaces, diverse mixed-income, mixed-use
            housing typologies, affordable to a wide range of community members, safe multi-modal mobility
            opportunities and access to transit. In addition, neighborhoods around The Heights District represent the
            spectrum of the City’s social and economic diversity with both affluent and economically vulnerable residents.
            The Heights District Plan is an opportunity for the COV to partner with the private sector to bring new
            investment to central Vancouver and ensure that new development provides benefits and opportunities to a
            broad range of residents and businesses now and into the future.

            The Heights District Plan is guided by policy and regulatory documents that provide specific guidance for the
            Project limits.


            Project Scope of Work
            The First Forty Feet Team will work with the City of Vancouver to provide public outreach and prepare the final
            master plan, construction drawings, specifications, cost estimates, permit documents and provide bidding and
            construction support.

            The Project will complete master planning, construction, and permitting documents, for the development of
            public infrastructure including roadways, utilities, public spaces, wayfinding, and transit amenities within the
            63-acre TMRA.

            The following scope of work tasks describes how the Consultant Team will collaborate with the COV project
            manager, city staff, key stakeholders, community members, and regulatory agencies to prepare the final
            masterplan, 30% design and Phase 1 Plan.

            Subtask 1.4: Quality Assurance/Quality Control
            The First Forty Feet Team will provide QA/QC for conceptual design, technical analyses, and construction
            documentation, specifications and permitting work in accordance with the Consultant’s QA/QC Program.
            The First Forty Team’s QA/QC will ensure appropriate, right-sized quality assurance and control measures are
            in place and executed at key points during planning and design efforts. Greg Jellison, of PBS will be the
            QA/QC manager who has worked extensively with the City of Vancouver on similar projects. The QA/QC
            process will be active throughout the life of the delivery process, providing a balance between the Design
            Confirmation (Tasks 2-4) and Design Implementation (Tasks 5-8) phases with technical reviewers involved to
            ensure that technical elements are accounted for during the Design Confirmation phase and that overarching
            themes of the masterplan are not lost during Design Implementation.

            The QA/QC plan will be integrated throughout all processes and woven into our critical path delivery
            schedule; for example, how the use of public spaces and multi-modal facilities throughout the project area will
            be vetted early in the Design Confirmation process will require that the design team support concepts and
            cost estimating processes with additional permitting requirements being accounted for. The First Forty Team
            will have the proper experts involved throughout the project life at varying capacity providing senior level
            design and construction personnel to review deliverables and provide technical support.

            Task 2: Communications Plan
            The First Forty Feet Team understands the COV will lead community engagement and communications on this
            project, serving as the face and the main contact for stakeholders and the community at large. The Consultant
            Team will coordinate, with the COV, identification of the necessary stakeholders, methods of outreach,
            engagement, and summary reporting, including a meeting schedule, and facilities or online applications
            necessary and available to support a range of in-person (if desired) and virtual engagement.
            The COV will manage delivery of project updates and information through the targeted use of established
            communications channels, such as the Heights District Plan email list, the City of Vancouver website and social
            media, Be Heard Vancouver engagement platform, Office of Neighborhoods and Vancouver Connects
            newsletters, and My Vancouver app.

            The First Forty Feet Team will prepare necessary planning, design, logistics, content and materials to support
            the COV in communications and outreach efforts.

            PBS, with FFF support, will prepare a Project Communications Plan in coordination with the COV
            Communications team to guide both how the project is communicated and how input is used and shared.
            with the purpose of:
                 •   Outlining the goals for public engagement.
                 •   Specifying the project design and programming elements stakeholder input will inform.
                •    Detailing methods, techniques, timelines and staffing assignments.

                          Stakeholder Identification
            The First Forty Feet Team recognizes the Heights District Plan is an opportunity for the COV to partner with
            the private sector to bring new investment to central Vancouver and ensure that new development provides
            benefits and opportunities to a broad range of residents and businesses now and into the future.

            Assumptions:
               • The following stakeholders are identified for engagement to provide direction, build excitement, be
                  inclusive, form/strengthen strategic partnerships and promote the public infrastructure’s community
                  benefits.

                       o    City Council
                            The City Council will be briefed on the project to review and provide feedback for the draft Field
                            Guide, Preliminary Concepts, Preferred Concept, and draft Place Guide.

                       o    Commissions
                            Commissions can provide insight and guidance for preliminary and preferred concepts with unique
                            perspectives, local knowledge and a commitment to advocacy for multi-modal access, the arts and
                            parks and recreational facilities. Commissions to consider include:
                               • Parks and Recreation Advisory Commission (PRAC)
                               • Urban Forestry Commission (UFC)
                               • Culture Arts and Heritage Commission (CAHC)
                               • Transportation and Mobility Commission (TMC)
                               • Aviation Advisory Committee (AAC)

                       o    Public Agencies
                            The City has a number of relevant public agencies to provide education, promote economic
                            development, housing affordability and services to seniors, people with disabilities, veterans and
                            other at-risk populations. PBS and FFF will consult with COV to determine public agencies for
                            potential engagement such as:
                               • C-TRAN,
                               • McLoughlin Middle School and George C. Marshall Elementary Schools,
                               • VHA

                       o    Community Based Organizations and Strategic Partners:
                             Targeted engagement with CBO's and other strategic partners will ensure equitable processes
                             and outcomes. This would be coordinated closely with the Equitable Development Plan. COV to
                             provide a list of appropriate CBO’s for potential engagement.

                       o    Affected Property Owners and Businesses:
                            Affected owners and businesses should be at the planning table to identify and address potential
                            impacts of design refinements and infrastructure phasing as well as, opportunities for
                            redevelopment and investment in the Tower Mall Redevelopment Area.

                       o    Universal accessibility advocates: The Heights District Plan project tapped into the sight impaired
                            community to gather accessibility insights--continuing this engagement will inform accessibility
                            and wayfinding strategies for the Master Plan refinement. COV to connect with School for the
                            Blind and School for the Deaf.

                           Project Engagement Milestones and Topics
            Engagement milestones will be the opportunities for engagement to identify a range of stakeholder
            perspectives to inform the Project’s preliminary and preferred concepts., public arts, gateways and wayfinding
            plan, interim and long-term public use area programming and on-site demonstration projects. Stakeholders
            will be given the opportunity to provide input so that the design of public infrastructure provides the most
            benefit to the communities it will serve.

            FFF and PBS will coordinate with the COV engagement with stakeholders at two Project milestones.
                •    Engagement Milestone #1 – Preliminary Concept Plans
                •    Engagement Milestone #2 - Preferred Concept Plan

            The FFF Team proposes two (2) engagement milestones with the Project stakeholders. Engagement Milestone
            #1 is intended to gather insights on preliminary public area (streets, plazas and parks) design concepts and
            alternatives; and Engagement Milestone #2 would review and provide feedback on the preferred public area
            (streets, plazas and parks) design concepts and alternatives. Engagement sessions will include one-on-one or
            group interviews, meetings, and feedback gathering through on-line surveys to be finalized in the Project’s
            Communications Plan.

            Assumptions:
               • Engagement sessions will be organized around three topics and aligned with appropriate stakeholder
                  participants.

                     1.    Transit and Multi-Modal Accessibility
                           Planned transit and multi-modal access improvements are extensive throughout the Project area.
                           Engagement can help inform the use and value for these new facilities to promote walk and bike
                           access to destinations, contribute to a complete network and offer a community benefit. The
                           Transportation and Mobility Commission (TMC), universal accessibility advocates, schools, Safe
                           Routes to School advocates, and Skyline Crest residents would be oriented to this topic.

                     2.    Parks, Plaza, and Grand Loop Use and Programming
                           The three-quarter mile Grand Loop consists of distinct segments providing an opportunity for
                           engagement to inform the function and form of those segments as they relate to adjacent uses as
                           well as the types of thematic and unifying elements that define the loop as a civic strolling and
